music_q1.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 1: Musical Instruments & Exponents

questions.question: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Bhajan Sopori are internationally renowned maestros of which Indian classical musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Bhajan Sopori are associated with the Santoor, a multi-stringed hammered dulcimer originating from the Sufiana musical tradition of Jammu & Kashmir.

questions.question: Ustad Bismillah Khan, who was conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2001, brought which instrument from royal courtyards and weddings to the classical concert stage?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bismillah Khan single-handedly elevated the Shehnai to classical concert stature. He performed at the Red Fort on the eve of India's independence on August 15, 1947.

questions.question: Which maestro is considered the pioneer of the 'Mohan Veena', a modified Hawaiian archtop guitar?
questions.explanation: Pandit Vishwa Mohan Bhatt created and patented the Mohan Veena, a 20-string modified slide guitar, and won a Grammy Award for his album 'A Meeting by the River'.

questions.question: Ustad Zakir Hussain, Pandit Kishan Maharaj, and Pandit Samta Prasad (Gudai Maharaj) are legendary exponents of which percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: All three are legendary tabla virtuosos: Zakir Hussain represents the Punjab gharana, while Kishan Maharaj and Samta Prasad belonged to the Benaras gharana.

questions.question: With which stringed instrument were Ustad Ali Akbar Khan and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan associated?
questions.explanation: Ustad Ali Akbar Khan (Maihar gharana) and Ustad Amjad Ali Khan (Gwalior Senia Bangash gharana) are world-renowned maestros of the Sarod.

questions.question: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh are celebrated virtuosos of which wind instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia and Pannalal Ghosh brought the North Indian bamboo flute (Bansuri) to global prominence in classical Hindustani music.

questions.question: Which instrument was played by Ustad Asad Ali Khan, one of the last masters of the Khandarbani style of Dhrupad?
questions.explanation: Ustad Asad Ali Khan was the foremost master of the Rudra Veena, the ancient tubular stringed instrument traditionally accompanying Dhrupad.

questions.question: Dr. L. Subramaniam, M.S. Gopalakrishnan, and T.N. Krishnan are eminent maestros of which instrument in Indian classical music?
questions.explanation: Dr. L. Subramaniam, M.S. Gopalakrishnan, and T.N. Krishnan are the 'Violin Trinity' of Carnatic classical music, with MS Gopalakrishnan also excelling in Hindustani music.

questions.question: Ustad Sultan Khan, Pandit Ram Narayan, and Ustad Sabri Khan are synonymous with which bowed string instrument?
questions.explanation: They are the greatest exponents of the Sarangi, traditionally used to accompany vocalists and renowned for its tonal proximity to the human voice.

questions.question: The 'Ghatam'—a percussion instrument consisting of an earthenware pot with copper and iron fillings—was popularized internationally by which Grammy-winning maestro?
questions.explanation: T.H. 'Vikku' Vinayakram brought the South Indian clay-pot percussion instrument Ghatam to global fame through the fusion band 'Shakti'.

questions.question: Uppalapu Srinivas (U. Srinivas) was a legendary child prodigy and maestro of which Western instrument adapted into Carnatic classical music?
questions.explanation: Mandolin U. Srinivas adapted the electric mandolin to the microtonal gamakas of Carnatic classical music, gaining worldwide acclaim.

questions.question: Which maestro was famous for playing the Carnatic classical Saxophone?
questions.explanation: Kadri Gopalnath pioneered the use of the saxophone in Carnatic classical music after custom-modifying the mouthpiece and keywork.

questions.question: Palghat Mani Iyer, Palani Subramania Pillai, and Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman are celebrated exponents of which primary South Indian rhythm instrument?
questions.explanation: The Mridangam is the premier rhythmic percussion instrument in Carnatic concerts, championed by doyens like Palghat Mani Iyer and Umayalpuram K. Sivaraman.

questions.question: Which percussion instrument made of a monitor lizard skin stretched on a circular wooden frame was popularized by G. Harishankar and V. Selvaganesh?
questions.explanation: The Kanjira is a small South Indian frame drum belonging to the tambourine family, producing remarkable deep bending pitch modulations.

questions.question: Ustad Vilayat Khan, Pandit Nikhil Banerjee, and Pandit Budhaditya Mukherjee are virtuosos of which classical instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Vilayat Khan (Imdadkhani/Etawah gharana) and Pandit Nikhil Banerjee (Maihar gharana) are two of the greatest sitar players of the 20th century.

questions.question: Annapurna Devi, daughter of Baba Allauddin Khan, was the undisputed doyenne of which rare plucked bass string instrument?
questions.explanation: Annapurna Devi was the master of the Surbahar, sometimes called the bass sitar, and guru to legends like Hariprasad Chaurasia and Nikhil Banerjee.

questions.question: Totaram Sharma, Pandit Gopal Das, and Ramashreya Pathak are exponents of which ancient barrel-shaped classical drum?
questions.explanation: The Pakhawaj is an ancient barrel-shaped, two-headed drum primarily used as the rhythmic accompaniment for Dhrupad and Haveli Sangeet.

questions.question: Which folk string instrument played with a bow made of horsehair is traditionally associated with Rajasthani folk bards (Bhopas)?
questions.explanation: The Ravanahatha, made of a coconut shell resonator and bamboo neck, is played by Bhopas to narrate the epic folklore of Pabuji in Rajasthan.

questions.question: Ustad Sakar Khan and Ghewar Khan are famous maestros of which ancient bowed string instrument of the Manganiyar community of Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: The Kamaicha is an ancient 17-string bowed instrument carved from a single piece of mango wood, exclusive to the hereditary Muslim Manganiyar bards.

questions.question: Which percussion instrument consists of a metal tongue placed between the player's teeth and plucked, producing a twanging resonance?
questions.explanation: The Morsing (known in Carnatic music) is a lamellophone wind-percussion instrument held between teeth and resonated by breathing.

questions.question: Pandit Chhannulal Mishra and Pandit Rajan-Sajan Mishra are celebrated exponents of which classical music tradition?
questions.explanation: Pandit Chhannulal Mishra and the Rajan-Sajan Mishra duo belong to the Benaras gharana, famous for Khayal, Thumri, Dadra, and Kajari.

questions.question: Nadaswaram, a double-reed wind instrument considered auspicious in South Indian temples, was mastered by which legendary duo?
options: Thiruvizhimizhalai Brothers / Karukurichi Arunachalam / Sheikh Chinna Moulana
questions.explanation: Sheikh Chinna Moulana and Karukurichi Arunachalam were legendary masters of the temple wind instrument Nadaswaram.

questions.question: Which classical string instrument has an ivory-inlaid resonator made of jackfruit wood and is dedicated to Goddess Saraswati?
questions.explanation: The Saraswati Veena is the quintessential fretted string instrument of Carnatic classical music, typically crafted from seasoned jackfruit timber.

questions.question: Buddhadev Das Gupta and Radhika Mohan Maitra are prominent masters of which instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Buddhadev Das Gupta was an acclaimed maestro of the Sarod, belonging to the Shahjahanpur tradition founded by Murad Ali Khan.

questions.question: Which folk instrument consists of two hollow wooden gourds with a single string, widely used by Baul singers of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Ektara is a one-stringed instrument commonly used by wandering mystic Baul and Fakir minstrels of West Bengal and Bangladesh.

music_q2.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 2: Classical Gharanas & Vocal Genres

questions.question: Which is considered the oldest of all the Khayal gharanas in Hindustani classical music?
questions.explanation: The Gwalior Gharana is regarded as the mother of all Khayal gharanas, founded by Ustad Nathan Pir Bakhsh and his grandsons Haddu, Hassu, and Nathu Khan in the 19th century.

questions.question: Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan were the founders of which celebrated Hindustani classical gharana?
questions.explanation: The Kirana Gharana (named after Kairana in Uttar Pradesh) was founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan and Abdul Wahid Khan, renowned for emotional alaap and slow note development.

questions.question: Bharat Ratna Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and Dr. Gangubai Hangal belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (awarded Bharat Ratna in 2008) and Gangubai Hangal were disciples of Sawai Gandharva in the Kirana gharana.

questions.question: The 'Rangeela Gharana' is another popular historical name for which vocal music gharana?
questions.explanation: The Agra Gharana, associated with Ustad Faiyaz Khan (who used the mudra 'Prem Piya') and Haji Sujan Khan, is known for its blend of Dhrupad-Dhamar and Khayal.

questions.question: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, famous for his thumri 'Yaad Piya Ki Aaye', was the doyen of which gharana?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bade Ghulam Ali Khan was the greatest figure of the Patiala Gharana, noted for high-velocity taans, intricate sargams, and soulful thumris.

questions.question: Sangeet Martand Pandit Jasraj, who passed away in 2020, belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Pandit Jasraj was the foremost torchbearer of the Mewati Gharana, founded by Ghagge Nazir Khan, and created the unique jugalbandi style 'Jasrangi'.

questions.question: Which gharana was founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan and is noted for complex, rare ragas (Anvat Ragas) and intricate phrasing?
questions.explanation: The Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana was founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan. Leading exponents include Kesarbai Kerkar, Mogubai Kurdikar, and Kishori Amonkar.

questions.question: Kishori Amonkar, hailed as 'Gaan Saraswati', was a legendary exponent of which vocal tradition?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan Kishori Amonkar was the premier exponent of the Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana, daughter of the legendary vocalist Mogubai Kurdikar.

questions.question: The 'Dagarvani' style in Indian classical music is exclusively associated with which ancient vocal genre?
questions.explanation: Dagarvani (practiced by the illustrious Dagar family, such as Zahiruddin and Wasifuddin Dagar) is one of the four traditional vanis of pure Dhrupad singing.

questions.question: What are the four traditional stylistic banis/vanis of Dhrupad singing originating from Raja Man Singh Tomar and Tansen's era?
questions.explanation: Dhrupad has four primary vanis: Gauharvani (founded by Tansen), Khandarvani (Raja Sammokhan Singh), Nauharvani (Sripat), and Dagarvani (Brij Chand).

questions.question: Girija Devi, affectionately known as the 'Queen of Thumri', was the leading luminary of which gharana?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan Girija Devi was the foremost representative of the Benaras Gharana, excelling in semi-classical forms like Thumri, Dadra, Chaiti, and Kajari.

questions.question: Which gharana is primarily known for the development of the 'Tappa' style of singing featuring rapid, intricate zigzag patterns?
options: Gwalior Gharana (pioneered by Mian Ghulam Nabi Shori)
questions.explanation: Tappa originated from the camel riders of Punjab and was refined into a classical genre by Mian Shori (Ghulam Nabi), becoming a specialty of Gwalior singers.

questions.question: Begum Akhtar (Akhtari Bai Faizabadi) was hailed by which epithet for her peerless mastery in ghazals, dadra, and thumri?
questions.explanation: Begum Akhtar was given the title 'Mallika-e-Ghazal' for her emotive rendering of Urdu poetry, Thumri, and Dadra.

questions.question: Ustad Amir Khan was the founder of which distinguished gharana known for meditative, slow-tempo (Vilambit) development?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amir Khan founded the Indore Gharana, blending elements of Kirana and Bhendibazaar gharanas into a deeply introspective style.

questions.question: Which vocal form in Hindustani classical music utilizes rhythmic mnemonic syllables (such as Nom-Tom, Ta, Na, Dere) in place of meaningful poetic lyrics?
questions.explanation: Tarana (traditionally attributed to Amir Khusrau) uses Persian and Arabic syllables alongside pakhawaj bols sung at a fast tempo (Drut).

questions.question: What rhythmic cycle (Taal) is traditionally used when singing the classical genre 'Dhamar'?
questions.explanation: Dhamar is a classical form sung during Holi festivities in Dhamar Taal, which has 14 beats with an asymmetrical 5+2+3+4 beat structure.

questions.question: The 'Sahaswan' gharana (often paired as Rampur-Sahaswan) was founded by which legendary musician from Uttar Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Rampur-Sahaswan Gharana was founded by Ustad Inayat Hussain Khan (son-in-law of Haddu Khan of Gwalior). Modern exponents include Rashid Khan.

questions.question: Ustad Rashid Khan, who was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2022 and passed away in 2024, belonged to which gharana?
questions.explanation: Padma Bhushan Ustad Rashid Khan was the great-grandson of Inayat Hussain Khan and the premier vocalist of the Rampur-Sahaswan Gharana.

questions.question: The 'Bhendibazaar Gharana' in Mumbai was founded by three brothers—Chhajju Khan, Nazir Khan, and Khadim Hussain Khan. What was its signature breathing technique?
options: Akar breathing allowing singing long passages in a single breath without pausing
questions.explanation: Bhendibazaar singers trained in 'Khandameru' mathematics and breath-control to articulate complex swara combinations smoothly in one single breath.

questions.question: Prabha Atre, who was honoured with the Padma Vibhushan in 2022, was a senior doyenne of which gharana?
questions.explanation: Dr. Prabha Atre was an illustrious vocalist and scholar of the Kirana Gharana, having trained under Sureshbabu Mane and Hirabai Barodekar.

questions.question: In Hindustani classical music, what is the musical scale of seven notes in ascending order called?
questions.explanation: Arohana is the ascending sequence of notes, while Avarohana is the descending sequence of notes in a Raga.

questions.question: How many basic musical notes (Swaras) constitute the Saptak in Indian music?
options: 7 Shuddha Swaras (Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni)
questions.explanation: The Saptak consists of 7 basic (Shuddha) notes: Shadja (Sa), Rishabha (Re), Gandhara (Ga), Madhyama (Ma), Panchama (Pa), Dhaivata (Dha), and Nishada (Ni).

questions.question: How many total notes (including Komal and Teevra variants) exist in an Indian classical octave (Saptak)?
options: 12 notes (7 Shuddha, 4 Komal: Re, Ga, Dha, Ni; and 1 Teevra: Ma)
questions.explanation: An octave has 12 notes: 7 natural (Shuddha), 4 flat (Komal Re, Ga, Dha, Ni), and 1 sharp (Teevra Ma). Sa and Pa are achala (immovable).

questions.question: Which text written by Bharata Muni around the 2nd century BCE is the foundational treatise on Indian music, dance, and drama?
questions.explanation: Bharata Muni's Natyashastra is the earliest comprehensive authority on dramaturgy, aesthetics (Rasa theory), and musical instruments (Avanaddha, Ghana, Sushira, Tata).

questions.question: Which 13th-century musicological treatise authored by Sarangadeva at the Yadava court of Devagiri is revered as the definitive text on both Hindustani and Carnatic systems?
questions.explanation: Sangita Ratnakara ('Ocean of Music') by Sarangadeva was written just before the divergence of North Indian (Hindustani) and South Indian (Carnatic) traditions.

music_q3.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 3: Carnatic Music, Trinity & Classical Theory

questions.question: Who is revered as the 'Pitamaha' (Father/Grandfather) of Carnatic Music for codifying its beginner pedagogical framework (Sarali Varisai)?
questions.explanation: Purandara Dasa (1484–1564), the Haridasa saint from Karnataka, framed the graded lessons (Sarali, Jantai, Alankara) in Mayamalavagowla raga used to this day.

questions.question: Who are collectively revered as the 'Trinity of Carnatic Music' (Sangeetha Trimurti), all born in the temple town of Tiruvarur?
options: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri
Purandara Dasa, Kanaka Dasa, and Vadiraja
questions.explanation: Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar, and Syama Sastri were 18th-century contemporaries born in Tiruvarur (Tamil Nadu) who revolutionized Carnatic composition.

questions.question: The famous 'Pancharatna Kritis' (Five Gems) in ragas Nata, Gaula, Arabhi, Varali, and Sri were composed by which saint-composer?
questions.explanation: Saint Tyagaraja composed the magnificent Ghana Raga Pancharatna Kritis in praise of Lord Rama, sung annually during the Tyagaraja Aradhana festival in Thiruvaiyaru.

questions.question: Which of the Trinity composed primarily in Sanskrit, used the mudra 'Guruguha', and incorporated Western band tunes into Nottuswara sahityas?
questions.explanation: Muthuswami Dikshitar composed intricate Sanskrit kritis featuring Kamalamba Navavarna songs and the nom-de-plume 'Guruguha'.

questions.question: Syama Sastri, the eldest of the Carnatic Trinity, was an ardent devotee of Goddess Kamakshi of Kanchipuram and used which signature mudra?
questions.explanation: Syama Sastri used the signature mudra 'Syamakrishna' and was famed for complex rhythmic structures (Tala) and the Anandabhairavi raga.

questions.question: How many fundamental parent scales (Melakarta Ragas) exist in the 72-Melakarta system of Carnatic music formulated by Venkatamakhin?
questions.explanation: Venkatamakhin formulated the 72 Melakarta (Janaka) parent raga scheme in his 17th-century treatise 'Chaturdandi Prakasika', divided into 12 Chakras.

questions.question: What is a derived or child raga born out of a parent Melakarta raga called in Carnatic music?
questions.explanation: A Janya Raga is a child scale derived from a Melakarta (Janaka) parent raga by omitting notes (Varjya) or adopting an irregular step pattern (Vakra).

questions.question: What are the three structural segments of a standard Carnatic musical composition (Kriti)?
questions.explanation: A Carnatic Kriti consists of Pallavi (the opening theme/refrain), Anupallavi (the second section), and Charanam (the stanza concluding the piece).

questions.question: Which Maharaja of Travancore was a prolific composer in six languages and established the Swathi Sangeethotsavam festival?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Swathi Thirunal (1813–1846) was a musical genius who composed over 400 pieces in Sanskrit, Malayalam, Hindi, Telugu, Kannada, and Tamil using the mudra 'Padmanabha'.

questions.question: Tallapaka Annamacharya (Annamayya) is celebrated for composing thousands of Sankeertanas in praise of which deity?
questions.explanation: Annamacharya (1408–1503) is revered as the 'Pada-kavitha Pitamaha' for composing over 32,000 Telugu and Sanskrit sankeertanas for Lord Venkateswara at Tirupati.

questions.question: What is the name of the annual Carnatic music festival held on the banks of river Cauvery in Tamil Nadu to commemorate Saint Tyagaraja?
questions.explanation: The Tyagaraja Aradhana takes place annually in January (Pushya Bahula Panchami) at his samadhi in Thiruvaiyaru, where hundreds of musicians render the Pancharatna Kritis in unison.

questions.question: Which Tamil calendar month (spanning mid-December to mid-January) is famous globally for the Chennai Music Season (Madras Music Academy)?
questions.explanation: The Chennai Margazhi Music Season, established in 1927 to commemorate the founding of the Music Academy, is one of the world's largest classical cultural festivals.

questions.question: M. Balamuralikrishna, a legendary Carnatic vocalist and innovator, invented several new ragas with only 3 or 4 notes, including which raga?
questions.explanation: Dr. M. Balamuralikrishna created unique ragas like Lavangi (4 notes: Sa, Re, Ma, Ni) and Mahati, winning the Padma Vibhushan and Chevalier of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres.

questions.question: Which Carnatic vocal stalwart was known as the 'Bhishma Pithamaha' of modern Carnatic concert music for establishing the standard modern concert format (Kutcheri paddhati)?
questions.explanation: Ariyakudi Ramanuja Iyengar (1889–1967) structured the modern concert format starting with a Varnam, followed by kritis, Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi, and lighter padams/thillanas.

questions.question: What is 'Ragam-Tanam-Pallavi' (RTP) in a Carnatic concert?
options: The ultimate test of a musician's improvisational skill, melodic elaboration, and rhythmic dexterity
questions.explanation: RTP is the centerpiece of a Carnatic music recital, featuring extensive raga alapana, tanam (rhythmic pulse without tala), and pallavi (complex rhythmic improvisation).

questions.question: What is the microtonal grace note or melodic oscillation around a musical note called in Indian classical music?
questions.explanation: Gamaka is the essential ornamental movement or pitch curve around a note; without gamakas, a Carnatic raga cannot be recognized.

questions.question: Which Carnatic maestro of the 20th century was renowned for singing with profound emotion (Bhava) and served as the Principal of Swathi Thirunal Music Academy?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan Semmangudi Srinivasa Iyer was hailed as the 'King of Carnatic Music' and trained legends like M.S. Subbulakshmi.

questions.question: Who popularized the fast-paced, breathless brigas and intellectual approach in Carnatic vocal music in the mid-20th century?
questions.explanation: G.N. Balasubramaniam (GNB) revolutionized Carnatic vocal music with dazzling speed, sophisticated sruti bhedam, and modern stage presentation.

questions.question: What is the fast-paced, concluding rhythmic dance piece in a Carnatic music concert, similar to the Hindustani Tarana?
questions.explanation: The Thillana is a vibrant concluding piece filled with jatis (rhythmic rhythmic syllables) composed by legends like Lalgudi Jayaraman and Balamuralikrishna.

questions.question: Which 14th-century music scholar authored the treatise 'Chaturdandi Prakasika' detailing the Melakarta system?
questions.explanation: Venkatamakhin detailed the 72 Melakarta scheme in his seminal 1660 Sanskrit treatise 'Chaturdandi Prakasika'.

questions.question: What is the primary difference in tuning between Hindustani classical music and Western music?
options: Indian music is based on Just Intonation (natural harmonics relative to a continuous drone/Tanpura), while Western music uses Equal Temperament
questions.explanation: Indian classical music is modal, relying on the tonic root note (Sa) provided by the Tanpura drone, allowing microtonal intervals (Shrutis).

questions.question: How many microtones (Shrutis) are recognized in the Indian classical octave according to the Natyashastra and Sangita Ratnakara?
questions.explanation: Ancient Indian musicological theory establishes 22 distinct shrutis (microtonal pitch intervals) within a single Saptak.

questions.question: What is the term used in Indian classical music for the mood, sentiment, or emotional essence evoked by a raga?
questions.explanation: Bharata's Rasa theory outlines nine primary emotional states (Navarasas: Shringara, Hasya, Karuna, Raudra, Veera, Bhayanaka, Bibhatsa, Adbhuta, and Shanta).

questions.question: Which raga in Hindustani classical music is traditionally sung in the morning to invoke solemnity and devotion?
questions.explanation: Raga Bhairav (using Komal Re and Komal Dha) is the archetype morning raga associated with dawn, serious reflection, and spiritual prayer.

questions.question: Which royal king of Rewa presented Tansen with jewels before Mughal Emperor Akbar invited Tansen to his court as one of the Navaratnas?
questions.explanation: Raja Ramachandra Singh of Rewa (Madhya Pradesh) was Tansen's early royal patron before Emperor Akbar summoned Tansen to Agra in 1562.

music_q4.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 4: Folk Music & Regional Traditions

questions.question: Teejan Bai and Ritu Verma are world-renowned exponents of which traditional narrative folk ballad art of Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation: Teejan Bai won the Padma Vibhushan for Pandwani, singing tales of the Mahabharata (particularly Bhima) with a tanpura in the dramatic Kapalik style.

questions.question: The 'Baul' and 'Bhatiali' folk music traditions, sung by boatmen and mystic mendicants, belong to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bauls are mystic minstrel singers of Bengal whose songs are recognized by UNESCO as Masterpieces of Intangible Heritage. Bhatiali is the song of river boatmen.

questions.question: Which classical-folk music style of Rajasthan is characterized by songs like 'Kesariya Balam Aao Ni Padharo Mhare Des'?
questions.explanation: Maand is Rajasthan's sophisticated folk-classical singing style developed in the royal courts of Bikaner, Jodhpur, and Jaisalmer (sung by Allah Jilai Bai).

questions.question: Allah Jilai Bai was a celebrated Rajasthani folk singer honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for which musical genre?
questions.explanation: Allah Jilai Bai immortalized the Rajasthani welcome ballad 'Kesariya Balam' in the Maand style.

questions.question: Which heroic ballad genre of Maharashtra was historically sung by Gondhalis and Shahirs to narrate the military exploits of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj?
questions.explanation: Powada is a dramatic Marathi ballad style composed by Shahirs (such as Agandas and Tulsidas) recounting battles and bravery of Maratha warriors.

questions.question: The fast-paced rhythmic song-and-dance form 'Lavani' of Maharashtra is traditionally accompanied by which percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: Lavani is driven by the sharp, energetic beats of the Dholki, performed by female dancers wearing nine-yard Nauvari sarees.

questions.question: Bihu Geet is the traditional folk song genre celebrating the agricultural cycle in which state?
questions.explanation: Bihu songs are performed in Assam during Bohag, Kati, and Magh Bihu, accompanied by the Dhol, Pepa (buffalo horn flute), and Gogona (bamboo jaw harp).

questions.question: Which traditional musical instrument of Assam is made from the horn of a domestic water buffalo?
questions.explanation: The Pepa is a double-reed wind instrument crafted from a horn of the Asiatic water buffalo, integral to Rongali Bihu music.

questions.question: Which monsoon folk song genre of Uttar Pradesh and Bihar depicts the longing of women during the rainy season and the swings of Saawan?
questions.explanation: Kajari is sung in the Bhojpuri and Awadhi regions during the monsoon month of Shravana, celebrating the arrival of rain and romance.

questions.question: Which folk musical form of Uttar Pradesh is sung during the spring month of Chaitra, often reflecting themes of Lord Rama?
questions.explanation: Chaiti is a semi-classical seasonal folk genre sung in the month of Chaitra (March-April), popular in Varanasi and eastern UP.

questions.question: The heroic folk ballad 'Alha-Khand' describing the battles of medieval warrior brothers Alha and Udal belongs to which region?
questions.explanation: Alha singing is a martial ballad tradition of Bundelkhand composed by Jagnik in praise of Chandel Rajput heroes Alha and Udal.

questions.question: Which oral storytelling musical theatre form of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana is performed by a troupe of three with a tambura and brass drums?
questions.explanation: Burra Katha (named after the 'burra' hollow shell drum) is a popular folk storytelling format using narrative, humor, and patriotic songs.

questions.question: The 'Villu Pattu' (Bow Song) is an ancient musical storytelling tradition belonging to which southern state?
questions.explanation: Villu Pattu uses a large bow strung with bells rested on an earthen pot, struck with sticks while singing mythological and social folklore.

questions.question: Which Sufi musical tradition popularized by Amir Khusrau and Baba Bulleh Shah is performed at shrines across Punjab, Delhi, and Rajasthan?
questions.explanation: Qawwali is a 700-year-old Sufi devotional tradition founded by Hazrat Amir Khusrau at the shrine of Nizamuddin Auliya in Delhi.

questions.question: Which legendary Pakistani-origin singer was internationally acclaimed as the 'Shahenshah-e-Qawwali' (King of Qawwali)?
questions.explanation: Ustad Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan popularized Qawwali across world music stages, collaborating with Western composers and popularizing Sufi mysticism.

questions.question: The devotional poems composed by Saint Kabir are popularly sung in which musical poetic format?
questions.explanation: Kabir's verses are composed as Dohas (couplets) and Sakhis, sung in the Nirgun folk bhajan tradition popularized by Kumar Gandharva.

questions.question: Which legendary Hindustani classical maestro of the 20th century was celebrated for resurrecting Kabir's Nirgun Bhajans and creating unique ragas?
questions.explanation: Kumar Gandharva, based in Dewas (MP), was an iconoclast genius who researched Malwa folk tunes and composed timeless Kabir bhajans.

questions.question: Which harvest folk music and dance of the Santhal tribal community is accompanied by the Madal and Tamak drums?
questions.explanation: Sohrai is the winter cattle-and-harvest festival of the Santhal tribe across Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal, accompanied by the earthenware Madal.

questions.question: Which folk musical tradition of Kashmir is performed with the Santoor and Saaz-e-Kashmir in Sufi gatherings?
questions.explanation: Sufiana Kalam is the classical choral music of Kashmir utilizing traditional Maqams, Persian poetry, and the 100-stringed Santoor.

questions.question: What is 'Chhakri' in Kashmiri folk music?
options: A popular choral folk song accompanied by the Sarangi, Rabab, and Noot (earthen pot)
questions.explanation: Chhakri is the most popular form of Kashmiri folk music, sung in groups during weddings and night-long gatherings.

questions.question: Which folk song tradition of Uttarakhand tells of love, separation, and farming in the Garhwal and Kumaon hills?
questions.explanation: Jhumelo, Khuder, and Chhopati are lyric folk songs of Uttarakhand expressing the pain of women separated from their maternal homes.

questions.question: The 'Mando' is a slow, elegant romantic song genre that developed among the Christian community of which state, blending Indian and Western melodies?
questions.explanation: Mando is a Goan musical form composed in Konkani, combining Portuguese guitar rhythms with traditional Konkani lyricism.

questions.question: Which rhythmic folk music of Ladakh is played on the Surna (oboe) and Daman (kettledrums) during monasteries and archery festivals?
questions.explanation: The Surna (wind instrument) and Daman (pair of bronze kettledrums) are the sacred instrumental ensemble of Ladakhi cultural life.

questions.question: What is 'Bhavageethe' in Karnataka and Maharashtra?
options: Light expressive emotional poetry set to melody (lyric poetry music)
questions.explanation: Bhavageethe ('emotion poetry') is popular in Karnataka and Maharashtra, setting modern lyric poetry (like Kuvempu and Bendre) to light music.

questions.question: Who is regarded as the legendary pioneer of Assamese modern music and cinema, composer of 'O Mur Apunar Desh'?
questions.explanation: Lakshminath Bezbaroa wrote Assam's state anthem 'O Mur Apunar Desh', while Jyoti Prasad Agarwala pioneered modern Assamese musical cinema.

music_q5.month_name: Set 5: Bharat Ratna & Sangeet Natak Akademi
music_q5.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 5: Bharat Ratna & Akademi Laureates

questions.question: Who was the very first musician to be awarded India's highest civilian honour, the 'Bharat Ratna', in 1998?
questions.explanation: Carnatic vocal queen Madurai Shanmukhavadivu Subbulakshmi was the first musician to receive the Bharat Ratna in 1998, and also the first Indian to perform at the UN General Assembly in 1966.

questions.question: In which year was sitar maestro Pandit Ravi Shankar awarded the Bharat Ratna?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar (Maihar gharana) was awarded the Bharat Ratna in 1999 for his unparalleled contributions in bridging Indian and Western classical music.

questions.question: Which two music stalwarts were jointly conferred the Bharat Ratna in 2001?
options: Lata Mangeshkar and Ustad Bismillah Khan
Pandit Bhimsen Joshi and M.S. Subbulakshmi
questions.explanation: In 2001, the Government of India conferred the Bharat Ratna on melody queen Lata Mangeshkar and Shehnai maestro Ustad Bismillah Khan.

questions.question: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was awarded the Bharat Ratna in which year?
questions.explanation: Kirana gharana legend Pandit Bhimsen Joshi was awarded the Bharat Ratna in November 2008, famous for his khayals and abhangs like 'Majhe Maher Pandhari'.

questions.question: The 'Bard of Brahmaputra', Dr. Bhupen Hazarika, was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in which year?
questions.explanation: Assamese singer, poet, and composer Dr. Bhupen Hazarika was posthumously awarded the Bharat Ratna in 2019 alongside Pranab Mukherjee and Nanaji Deshmukh.

questions.question: Which prestigious international award was won five times by Pandit Ravi Shankar for his collaborative albums?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar won five Grammy Awards, including the Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2013.

questions.question: Who was the first Indian to win an Academy Award (Oscar) in 1983 for Costume Design in the film 'Gandhi'?
questions.explanation: Bhanu Athaiya made history as the first Indian to win an Oscar for designing costumes for Richard Attenborough's biopic 'Gandhi'.

questions.question: In 2009, music composer A.R. Rahman won two Academy Awards (Oscars) for which film?
options: Slumdog Millionaire (Best Original Score and Best Original Song 'Jai Ho')
questions.explanation: A.R. Rahman won two Oscars for 'Slumdog Millionaire' for Best Original Score and Best Original Song ('Jai Ho'), alongside sound designer Resul Pookutty.

questions.question: The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's National Academy for Music, Dance and Drama, was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi was established in 1953 by the Ministry of Education, functioning as the apex body for performing arts in India.

questions.question: Where are the headquarters of the Sangeet Natak Akademi located?
options: Rabindra Bhavan, Copernicus Marg, New Delhi
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi is headquartered at Rabindra Bhavan in New Delhi.

questions.question: What is the highest honour conferred by the Sangeet Natak Akademi, restricted to a maximum of 40 living fellows at any time?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (Akademi Ratna) is the most prestigious lifetime award in performing arts, limited to 40 living recipients.

questions.question: Which award is conferred annually by the Sangeet Natak Akademi to young artists under the age of 40 years?
questions.explanation: The Ustad Bismillah Khan Yuva Puraskar was introduced in 2006 to encourage outstanding young artists in music, dance, and theatre.

questions.question: The prestigious annual 'Tansen Samman' in classical music is conferred by which state government?
questions.explanation: The Government of Madhya Pradesh awards the National Tansen Samman every December during the World Sangeet Tansen Festival in Gwalior.

questions.question: Where is the historic tomb (Samadhi) of Sangeet Samrat Mian Tansen located?
questions.explanation: Tansen's tomb is located in Gwalior near the mausoleum of his Sufi spiritual mentor Sheikh Muhammad Ghaus.

questions.question: The prestigious 'Kalidas Samman' for classical music, classical dance, theatre, and visual arts is instituted by which state government?
questions.explanation: The Government of Madhya Pradesh established the National Kalidas Samman in 1980, named after the classical Sanskrit writer Kalidasa.

questions.question: Which state government confers the 'Lata Mangeshkar Award' for lifetime achievement in music?
questions.explanation: Both Madhya Pradesh (her birthplace in Indore) and Maharashtra institute prestigious annual National Lata Mangeshkar Awards.

questions.question: What was the legendary singer Lata Mangeshkar's original birth name?
questions.explanation: Born in Indore in 1929, she was initially named Hema by her parents Pandit Deenanath Mangeshkar and Shevanti, and later renamed Lata.

questions.question: In 1963, Lata Mangeshkar moved Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru to tears by singing which patriotic song composed by C. Ramchandra?
options: Aye Mere Watan Ke Logo (written by Kavi Pradeep)
questions.explanation: Lata Mangeshkar performed 'Aye Mere Watan Ke Logo' at the National Stadium in Delhi on Republic Day 1963 following the 1962 Sino-Indian War.

questions.question: Which playback singer holds the Guinness World Record for recording the highest number of songs in history (over 40,000 songs in 16 languages)?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan S.P. Balasubrahmanyam recorded over 40,000 songs in a career spanning more than five decades across multiple Indian languages.

questions.question: K.J. Yesudas, known as the 'Celestial Singer' (Gana Gandharvan), has won the National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer how many times?
questions.explanation: Dr. K.J. Yesudas holds the all-time record of winning 8 National Film Awards for Best Male Playback Singer across Malayalam, Hindi, and Telugu.

questions.question: Who composed the iconic tune of the patriotic national song 'Mile Sur Mera Tumhara' broadcast on Doordarshan in 1988?
options: Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (composed by Ashok Patki & arranged by Louis Banks)
questions.explanation: The iconic national integration anthem 'Mile Sur Mera Tumhara' was conceived by Lok Seva Sanchar Parishad, anchored by Pandit Bhimsen Joshi.

questions.question: Which classical musician composed the music for Satyajit Ray's celebrated film 'The Apu Trilogy' (Pather Panchali)?
questions.explanation: Pandit Ravi Shankar composed the haunting, rustic sitar and flute musical score for Satyajit Ray's masterpiece 'Pather Panchali' (1955).

questions.question: The famous music director duo 'Shiv-Hari' in Hindi cinema (Silsila, Chandni, Darr) comprised which two classical legends?
options: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma (Santoor) and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia (Flute)
questions.explanation: Pandit Shivkumar Sharma and Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia teamed up as the composer duo 'Shiv-Hari', producing classic Bollywood melodies.

questions.question: Which music director duo 'Jatin-Lalit' belonged to the illustrious family of which classical Mewati gharana doyen?
questions.explanation: Composers Jatin and Lalit Pandit (and their sister Sulakshana Pandit) are the nephews of classical vocalist Pandit Jasraj.

questions.question: Which maestro was given the title 'Aftab-e-Mausiqi' (Sun of Music) by the royal court of Baroda in 1908?
questions.explanation: Maharaja Sayajirao Gaekwad III of Baroda conferred the title 'Aftab-e-Mausiqi' upon Ustad Faiyaz Khan of the Agra Gharana.

music_q6.month_name: Set 6: SSC CGL Recent PYQ Compilation
music_q6.title: SSC CGL Music PYQ - Set 6: 2021-2024 Exam PYQs

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022/2023: 'Padma Subrahmanyam' is associated with which Indian dance-music form?
questions.explanation: Dr. Padma Subrahmanyam is an eminent Bharatanatyam dancer, music composer, and indologist, conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2024.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Ustad Bundu Khan' and 'Santosh Mishra' are associated with which musical instrument?
questions.explanation: Ustad Bundu Khan (Delhi gharana) and Pandit Santosh Mishra are renowned exponents of the Sarangi.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Zakir Hussain' is the son of which legendary tabla player of the Punjab gharana?
questions.explanation: Ustad Zakir Hussain is the eldest son of Ustad Alla Rakha Qureshi, who regularly accompanied Pandit Ravi Shankar.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: Which musical instrument was played by the famous musician 'Ustad Vilayat Khan'?
questions.explanation: Ustad Vilayat Khan was a titan of the Sitar who pioneered the 'Gayaki Ang' (imitating vocal nuances on the sitar).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Shovana Narayan' is a renowned master of which classical dance-music genre?
questions.explanation: Padma Shri Shovana Narayan is a distinguished Kathak dancer and disciple of Pandit Birju Maharaj.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Sitar' is classified under which ancient instrument category according to the Natyashastra?
questions.explanation: Bharata's Natyashastra classifies instruments into 4 groups: Tata (strings), Sushira (winds), Avanaddha (membranophones/drums), and Ghana (solid idiophones/bells).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: Drums like the Tabla and Mridangam fall under which category of musical instruments?
questions.explanation: Avanaddha Vadya refers to percussion instruments where animal skin or parchment is stretched over a hollow wooden or earthen vessel.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: Solid non-drum instruments like Manjira, Jhanj, and Ghatam fall under which Natyashastra category?
questions.explanation: Ghana Vadya are solid resonant instruments made of wood or metal played by striking, clashing, or shaking, needing no tuning.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: Wind instruments like the Bansuri, Shehnai, and Nadaswaram belong to which category?
questions.explanation: Sushira Vadya are aerophones or wind instruments where sound is generated by vibrating a column of air inside a tube.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Pandit Anindo Chatterjee' and 'Bikram Ghosh' are renowned exponents of which percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: Pandit Anindo Chatterjee and Bickram Ghosh are acclaimed tabla maestros of the Farrukhabad and Punjab gharanas.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Sangeet Natak Akademi Award' winner 'Guru Bipin Singh' was a legendary guru of which classical dance and music?
questions.explanation: Guru Bipin Singh is revered as the 'Father of Modern Manipuri Dance' and directed the Govindji Nartanalaya in Imphal.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Pt. Birju Maharaj', who passed away in 2022, was the torchbearer of which Kathak gharana?
questions.explanation: Pandit Birju Maharaj (Brijmohan Nath Mishra) was the doyen of the Kalka-Bindadin Lucknow gharana, son of Achchan Maharaj.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Sitara Devi' was described as 'Nritya Samragni' (Empress of Dance) by Rabindranath Tagore for her mastery in:
questions.explanation: Sitara Devi (Benaras gharana of Kathak) was given the title 'Nritya Samragni' by Rabindranath Tagore at the age of 16.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Ranjan-Sajan Mishra' who received the Padma Bhushan were brothers famous for singing in which style?
questions.explanation: Pandit Rajan and Sajan Mishra were celebrated for their synchronized vocal Jugalbandi in the Benaras khayal tradition.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: Which musical instrument is played by the maestro 'Ustad Amjad Ali Khan' and his sons Amaan and Ayaan Ali Bangash?
questions.explanation: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan and his sons represent the sixth and seventh generations of the Bangash-Senia Sarod gharana.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Kanak Rele' was a renowned dance scholar and performer instrumental in the revival of which classical dance?
questions.explanation: Padma Bhushan Dr. Kanak Rele founded the Nalanda Dance Research Centre in Mumbai, pioneering scientific choreography in Mohiniyattam.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'V. Satyanarayana Sarma' was an eminent performer of which classical dance tradition?
questions.explanation: Vedantam Satyanarayana Sarma was a master of Kuchipudi, especially celebrated for playing female roles such as Satyabhama.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Sattriya' dance, created by Mahapurusha Sankaradeva, was recognized as a classical dance by Sangeet Natak Akademi in which year?
questions.explanation: The Sangeet Natak Akademi officially recognized the 500-year-old Vaishnavite dance form Sattriya of Assam as India's 8th classical dance in the year 2000.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Kelucharan Mohapatra' was the architect of modern revival of which classical dance form?
questions.explanation: Padma Vibhushan Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra revived the Gotipua-rooted classical Odissi dance, establishing the premier institute 'Srjan'.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Rukmini Devi Arundale' founded which premier institution for classical Bharatanatyam in Chennai in 1936?
questions.explanation: Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra at Adyar (now Thiruvanmiyur), Chennai, restoring social respectability to the ancient dance Sadir (Bharatanatyam).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: Who was the founder of 'Kerala Kalamandalam' in 1930 to preserve the dying arts of Kathakali and Mohiniyattam?
questions.explanation: Poet laureate Vallathol Narayana Menon established Kerala Kalamandalam at Cheruthuruthy, reviving the temple arts of Kathakali, Koodiyattam, and Mohiniyattam.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: Which is the only Sanskrit theatre tradition of Kerala recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of Oral and Intangible Heritage?
questions.explanation: Koodiyattam, performed in temple theatres (Koothambalams) by the Chakyar and Nambiar communities, was the first Indian art form recognized by UNESCO in 2001.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Pandit Jasraj' pioneered which unique concept of male-female voice jugalbandi sung in different ragas simultaneously?
questions.explanation: Jasrangi is a novel duet format devised by Pt. Jasraj where a male and female singer sing in their natural pitch octaves using the principle of Murchhana.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Hassu Khan, Haddu Khan, and Nathu Khan' were historical master vocalists of which courtly gharana?
questions.explanation: They served as court musicians to the Maharaja of Gwalior, establishing the definitive open-throated, energetic Khayal style.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2024: Who is the first Indian woman to win two Grammy Awards, winning for her work on 'Slumdog Millionaire' with A.R. Rahman?
questions.explanation: Singer Tanvi Shah won a Grammy Award for writing the Spanish lyrics for 'Jai Ho' in Slumdog Millionaire, becoming the first Indian woman Grammy laureate.

dance_q1.title: SSC CGL Dance PYQ - Set 1: Dances of North India

questions.question: The 'Kalbelia' dance, recognized by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2010, belongs to which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kalbelia is a folk dance of the snake-charmer Kalbelia community of Rajasthan. Female dancers wear flowing black skirts (Lehenga) mimicking the graceful movements of a serpent.

questions.question: Who is the world-renowned exponent who popularized the Rajasthani Kalbelia dance on international stages and was awarded the Padma Shri?
questions.explanation: Gulabo Sapera overcame severe childhood adversity to single-handedly globalize the Kalbelia dance form.

questions.question: Which Rajasthani folk dance involves women balancing a stack of 7 to 9 brass or earthen pots on their head while dancing on the edge of a sword or brass plate?
questions.explanation: Bhavai is a thrilling balancing dance of Rajasthan (also performed in Gujarat) where female dancers balance multiple lit or water-filled brass pitchers.

questions.question: The 'Ghoomar' dance was originally developed by which indigenous tribal community of Rajasthan to worship Goddess Saraswati?
questions.explanation: Ghoomar was originally developed by the Bhil community and later embraced by Rajput royal households, characterized by pirouetting ghaghras.

questions.question: The 'Terah Taali' (Thirteen Cymbals) folk dance, where 13 cymbals (Manjiras) are tied to different parts of the female dancer's body, is performed by which community?
options: Kamar (Kammad) tribe in honour of folk deity Baba Ramdevji
questions.explanation: Terah Taali is a unique sitting dance of the Kamar tribe of Rajasthan performed at the Ramdevra fair near Pokhran.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Rajasthan involves dummy horses made of bamboo and papier-mâché, depicting mock battles of Rajput warriors?
questions.explanation: Kachhi Ghodi is a vibrant martial folk dance originating in the Shekhawati region of Rajasthan, performed during weddings and social celebrations.

questions.question: The 'Nati' dance, which entered the Guinness Book of World Records as the largest folk dance in the world, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Nati is the traditional group circle dance of Himachal Pradesh, celebrating Dussehra and harvest festivals in the Kullu valley.

questions.question: Which masked ritual dance is performed by Buddhist Lamas in monasteries across Ladakh, Himachal Pradesh, and Sikkim to drive away evil spirits?
questions.explanation: Chham is a sacred Tibetan Buddhist ritual mask dance accompanied by cymbals, conch shells, and long horns (Dungchen).

questions.question: The graceful 'Rouf' (Rauf) dance, performed by women facing each other in two rows with arms interlocked, is the traditional folk dance of:
questions.explanation: Rouf is a spring dance of the Kashmir valley, performed by women during Eid and the onset of pleasant spring weather.

questions.question: Which ritualistic folk dance of Jammu & Kashmir is performed exclusively by men of the Wattal tribe wearing long robes and tall conical caps?
questions.explanation: Dumhal is performed on special ceremonial occasions by men of the Wattal community around an auspicious banner stuck into the ground.

questions.question: The 'Shondol' dance, which entered the Guinness World Records for the largest Ladakhi dance, is known as:
options: The Royal Dance of Ladakh (performed for the King of Ladakh)
questions.explanation: Shondol was historically performed by royal female dancers to honor the King of Ladakh on auspicious occasions.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Punjab is performed exclusively by women, featuring claps, snaps, and joyful couplets (Boliyan)?
questions.explanation: Giddha is the female counterpart to Bhangra in Punjab, known for its spirited, rhythmic claps and energetic celebration of domestic life.

questions.question: The 'Kikli' dance in Punjab and Haryana is performed by:
options: Pairs of young girls crossing hands, locking arms, and twirling in fast circles
questions.explanation: Kikli is a popular folk game-dance of young girls who link arms and spin around at high speed while singing playful songs.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Haryana is named after the jewellery ornament worn on the forehead of women?
questions.explanation: The Jhoomar dance of Haryana (and parts of Punjab) takes its name from the forehead ornament 'Jhoomar' due to the rhythmic swaying movement of the dancers.

questions.question: The 'Loor' dance in Haryana is performed during which festive season?
options: During the festival of Holi (in the month of Phalguna)
questions.explanation: Loor is performed by women in Haryana around the Holi festival, deriving its name from the local word 'Loor' meaning 'girl'.

questions.question: Which ancient folk dance of Haryana traces its origins to the Mahabharata and is performed to the beat of the duff, dhol, and thali?
questions.explanation: Dhamal is an energetic celebratory folk dance of Haryana, historically performed by farmers on moonlit nights after a bountiful harvest.

questions.question: The 'Chholiya' (Choliya) dance, featuring dancers armed with swords and brass shields dressed as medieval martial warriors, belongs to which region?
questions.explanation: Chholiya is a 1,000-year-old martial sword dance of the Khas Rajput community in the Kumaon hills of Uttarakhand, performed in wedding processions.

questions.question: Which folk dance of the Garhwal region of Uttarakhand enacts scenes from the Mahabharata and Ramayana with masks, recognized by UNESCO in 2009?
options: Ramman (Religious festival and ritual theatre of Garhwal)
questions.explanation: Ramman is an annual ritual theatre and masked dance festival celebrated in the village of Saloor-Dungra in Chamoli district, Uttarakhand.

questions.question: The 'Charkula' dance, where women balance a multi-tiered wooden pyramid with 108 illuminated oil lamps on their heads, belongs to which cultural region?
questions.explanation: Charkula is a spectacular folk dance of the Braj region (Mathura-Vrindavan) of UP, commemorating the birth of Radha.

questions.question: Which traditional theatre-dance form of Uttar Pradesh depicts the romantic and divine childhood pastimes of Lord Krishna and Radha?
questions.explanation: Raslila is the devotional classical-folk dance drama of Mathura and Vrindavan celebrating the Raas of Radha and Krishna.

questions.question: The operatic musical folk theatre of North India characterized by high-pitched singing, drums (Naggara), and secular satire is called:
questions.explanation: Nautanki is the premier folk theatre of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and Rajasthan, based on historical romances like Laila-Majnu and Harishchandra.

questions.question: The 'Dangi' dance belongs to which district/region of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Dangi is a graceful female folk dance performed during harvest season in the Chamba valley of Himachal Pradesh.

questions.question: Which dance of Ladakh is performed by male warriors holding decorated swords to celebrate historical victories?
questions.explanation: Spao is the warrior dance of Ladakh, where dancers reenact archery and sword-fighting battle manoeuvres.

questions.question: The 'Jhora' dance of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh is performed in:
options: A large circular formation with dancers holding each other's shoulders and stepping in unison
questions.explanation: Jhora is an inclusive community circle dance of the Kumaon hills performed across castes during fairs and weddings.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Uttar Pradesh is performed to celebrate the birth of a male child in the family, with a brass plate (Thali) beaten rhythmically?
questions.explanation: Chhathi and Sohar songs accompanied by dances celebrate the sixth day after childbirth in North Indian households.

dance_q2.title: SSC CGL Dance PYQ - Set 2: Dances of East & Northeast India

questions.question: The 'Bagurumba' folk dance, famously known as the 'Butterfly Dance' due to its colorful attire mimicking fluttering wings, belongs to which tribe of Assam?
questions.explanation: Bagurumba is the iconic traditional dance of the Bodo community in Assam, performed by young women wearing brightly colored Dokhona and Jwmgra scarves.

questions.question: Which community of Tripura performs the acrobatic 'Hojagiri' dance, balancing an earthen pitcher on the head and lamps on the hands?
questions.explanation: Hojagiri is the signature dance of the Reang tribe of Tripura, characterized by pitch-perfect hip undulations while balancing pitchers and bottles.

questions.question: The famous 'Cheraw' dance, popularly known as the 'Bamboo Dance', is the traditional folk dance of which state?
questions.explanation: Cheraw is the ancient rhythmic dance of Mizoram where male performers tap horizontal bamboo staves while female dancers step in and out of the closing grids.

questions.question: Which martial dance of Manipur features simulated combat using traditional spears (Ta) and curved swords (Thang)?
questions.explanation: Thang-Ta is the traditional armed martial art dance of the Meitei people of Manipur, integrated into physical fitness and rituals.

questions.question: The 'Pung Cholom' (Drum Dance) is an acrobatic dance of Manipur performed with which cylindrical percussion instrument?
questions.explanation: Pung Cholom dancers play the Pung drum while performing breathtaking airborne leaps, acrobatics, and synchronous rhythmic spins.

questions.question: The 'Lai Haraoba' festival dance of Manipur, celebrating the creation of the cosmos, is performed before which local village deities?
questions.explanation: Lai Haraoba ('Festivity of the Gods') is celebrated by the Meitei community to propitiate the Umang Lai deities, led by female priestesses called Maibis.

questions.question: The 'Chhau' dance, recognized by UNESCO in 2010, is practiced in three distinct regional sub-styles across Eastern India. What are they?
options: Purulia Chhau (WB), Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha), and Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand)
questions.explanation: Chhau has three styles: Seraikella and Purulia use stylized clay/papier-mâché masks, while Mayurbhanj Chhau is performed without masks.

questions.question: The 'Gotipua' dance of Odisha, where young boys dress as women to praise Lord Jagannath, is the historical precursor to which classical dance?
questions.explanation: Gotipua ('single boy') dancers perform acrobatic bandhas in temples; modern Odissi gurus like Kelucharan Mohapatra started as Gotipua dancers.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Odisha is named after a round earthen pitcher used as a musical drum and was historically a war dance of the Kalahandi region?
questions.explanation: Ghumura is a vibrant martial folk dance of Kalahandi, Odisha, where performers tie the Ghumura pitcher-drum to their chest while dancing.

questions.question: The 'Ranappa' dance of Ganjam district in Odisha is unique because the performers dance on:
questions.explanation: Ranappa ('stilts') is an energetic acrobatic dance performed by young men balanced on high bamboo stilts, depicting Lord Krishna's childhood deeds.

questions.question: Which folk dance of Jharkhand involves male dancers dressed as warriors holding shields and spears in a mock martial battle?
questions.explanation: Paika was historically practiced by Munda and tribal warrior-guards (Paikas) of Jharkhand and Odisha to develop physical agility for battle.

questions.question: The 'Karma' dance, celebrated by the Gond, Baiga, Oraon, and Munda tribes across Central and Eastern India, is named after:
options: The sacred Karma tree (Nauclea parvifolia / Kadam)
questions.explanation: The Karma dance is performed during the autumn harvest in honour of Karma Devta, symbolized by a branch of the sacred Karma tree.

questions.question: Which dance of the Garo tribe in Meghalaya is celebrated during the post-harvest '100 Drums Festival'?
questions.explanation: The Wangala dance is performed to thank the Sun God Misi Saljong, with 100 long cylindrical drums beaten in thunderous synchronization.

questions.question: The 'Shad Suk Mynsiem' (Dance of Peaceful Hearts) is the thanksgiving spring festival dance of which indigenous tribe of Meghalaya?
questions.explanation: Shad Suk Mynsiem is celebrated by the Khasi people in Shillong every spring, honoring God (U Blei) for prosperity, health, and rain.

questions.question: The 'Nongkrem' dance festival of Meghalaya, featuring the Pomblang goat sacrifice, is celebrated at which royal seat?
options: Smit (the cultural capital of the Khyrim Syiemship)
questions.explanation: Nongkrem is celebrated by the Khasi people at Smit to propitiate Goddess Ka Blei Synshar for rich crop harvests.

questions.question: The 'Singhi Chham' (Snow Lion Dance) and 'Yak Chham' are iconic cultural folk dances belonging to which Himalayan state?
questions.explanation: Singhi Chham represents the mythical white snow lion, the sacred guardian of Mount Khangchendzonga, revered by the Bhutia people of Sikkim.

questions.question: The 'Chang Lo' (Sua Lua) folk dance, celebrating victory over enemies, is performed by which Naga tribe of Nagaland?
questions.explanation: The Chang Lo dance is performed by the Chang tribe of Nagaland during the Poanglem festival over three days.

questions.question: The 'Ponung' dance, performed exclusively by women dancing in a tight circle to the rhythm of the 'Yoksha' sword rattle, belongs to which tribe of Arunachal Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Ponung dance is performed by young Adi women in Arunachal Pradesh during harvest celebrations, guided by a lead singer (Miri).

questions.question: Which folk dance of the Digaru Mishmi tribe of Arunachal Pradesh is performed during the 'Tamladu' festival to ward off evil spirits?
questions.explanation: Buiya is a celebratory tribal dance of the Digaru Mishmi community, performed in community halls after agricultural festivals.

questions.question: The 'Bardo Chham' dance of Arunachal Pradesh portrays which universal theme?
options: The victory of good over evil (represented by dancers wearing animal masks)
questions.explanation: Bardo Chham is performed by the Sherdukpen community of West Kameng, enacting legends of good spirits vanquishing evil animal-like demons.

questions.question: Which famous folk dance of West Bengal is performed with wooden masks during the Charak festival in the Malda district?
questions.explanation: Gambhira is a masked devotional folk performance of North Bengal addressed to Lord Shiva, incorporating social satire.

questions.question: The 'Brita' (Vrita) dance of West Bengal is traditionally performed by women for which purpose?
options: As a thanksgiving to deities after recovering from dangerous diseases like smallpox or childbirth
questions.explanation: Brita dance is a ritualistic thanksgiving dance by village women after their families survive epidemics or achieve childbirth blessings.

questions.question: The 'Jhumur' dance, performed with interconnected arms and swinging footwork, is the quintessential folk dance of which community across Assam and West Bengal?
options: Tea garden worker communities (Adivasi tea tribes)
questions.explanation: Jhumur is celebrated by the tea garden labourers of Assam and North Bengal during autumn and spring festivals.

questions.question: Which dance of Tripura is performed during the harvest of cotton crops?
questions.explanation: Mamita is celebrated by the Jamatia and Tripuri tribes to rejoice after completing the autumn cotton harvest.

questions.question: The 'Bizu' (Biju) dance is the festive spring New Year dance of which tribal community in Tripura and the Chittagong Hill Tracts?
questions.explanation: Bizu is the most important cultural dance festival of the Buddhist Chakma community, marking the transition into the New Year.

dance_q3.title: SSC CGL Dance PYQ - Set 3: Dances of Central & Western India

questions.question: The 'Garba' dance of Gujarat, recognized by UNESCO on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2023, is performed during which festival?
questions.explanation: Garba is an ancient circular devotional dance dedicated to Goddess Amba, performed around a perforated earthen lamp (Garbha Deep) during the nine nights of Navratri.

questions.question: The 'Tippani' folk dance, where women beat the floor with long wooden sticks attached to iron blocks, originated among female laborers of which region of Gujarat?
questions.explanation: Tippani originated among female laborers of the Koli and Kharva communities of Chorwad who used 'tippani' rammers to beat and level lime concrete roofs.

questions.question: The 'Bhavai' folk theatre and dance of Gujarat and Rajasthan was created in the 14th century by which poet-playwright?
questions.explanation: Asaita Thakar, an outcast Brahmin scholar, created the satirical Bhavai theatre consisting of quick dramatic sketches (Veshas).

questions.question: Which energetic folk dance of Maharashtra is performed during Ganeshotsav and school displays with small wooden batons fitted with metallic jingles?
questions.explanation: Lezim is a high-energy rhythmic fitness and dance form of Maharashtra, driven by the metallic clinking of the lezim instrument and the dhol.

questions.question: The 'Koli' dance of Maharashtra portrays the occupational lifestyle, boat rowing, and wave-catching of which community?
options: Fisherfolk (Koli community) of the Konkan coast
questions.explanation: Koli dance is performed by fisherwomen and fishermen of Mumbai and Konkan, depicting sea voyages, casting nets, and hauling fish.

questions.question: The 'Dhangari Gaja' dance of Maharashtra is the traditional pastoral dance of which sheep-rearing shepherd community?
questions.explanation: Dhangari Gaja is performed by Dhangar shepherds of Solapur and Western Maharashtra in honor of their tutelary deity Biruba (Biroba).

questions.question: Which dramatic theatrical folk performance of Maharashtra involves narrative humor, dialogue, and Lavani songs, patronized by the Peshwas in the 18th century?
questions.explanation: Tamasha (from the Persian word for fun/show) reached its zenith under Peshwa Baji Rao II, blending Bheel poetry with classical musical storytelling.

questions.question: The 'Gondhal' ritual dance-drama of Maharashtra and Karnataka is performed to invoke the blessings of which deities during weddings?
options: Goddess Bhavani of Tuljapur / Mahalakshmi of Kolhapur
questions.explanation: Gondhal is an ancient thanksgiving ritual performed by Gondhali minstrels after major life milestones like weddings or thread ceremonies.

questions.question: The 'Matki' dance, where women dance with earthen pots stacked on their heads to the rhythm of the Dhol, belongs to which region of Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Matki is a solo and group folk dance of women in the Malwa plateau, performed during wedding celebrations.

questions.question: Which harvest folk dance of the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh features women balancing baskets full of sprouted green jowar crops on their heads?
questions.explanation: Jawara is performed by farmers of Bundelkhand to invoke Goddess Bhavani's blessings for agricultural prosperity and rain.

questions.question: The 'Maanch' is the traditional lyrical folk theatre and musical dance form belonging to which state?
questions.explanation: Maanch (meaning 'stage') was created in Ujjain and Malwa around 300 years ago, featuring heroic folk legends and operatic musical exchanges.

questions.question: The 'Saila' (Sela) dance, where young men strike small bamboo sticks together in rhythmic synchronization, is performed by tribal communities in:
questions.explanation: Saila is a stick dance of the Baiga and Gond tribes celebrating post-harvest leisure across the central Indian tribal belt.

questions.question: The 'Raut Nacha' folk dance of Chhattisgarh is celebrated by the Yadav (Raut) community during which festival?
questions.explanation: Raut Nacha depicts the battle between King Kamsa and Lord Krishna, performed by cowherd Yaduvanshis armed with sticks and shields during Diwali.

questions.question: The 'Panthi' dance of Chhattisgarh is the spiritual and ritual dance of which social reform community?
questions.explanation: Panthi dancers sing the Nirgun spiritual verses of Baba Guru Ghasidas, performing astonishing human pyramids and gymnastics.

questions.question: The 'Sua' (Suwa) or Parrot dance, performed by Baiga and Gond women clapping small wooden parrots, belongs to:
questions.explanation: In the Sua dance, women dance around a basket containing a wooden green parrot (symbolizing messenger of love) while singing folklore.

questions.question: The 'Fugdi' folk dance, where women perform in circles and blow into their hands making a 'foo' sound at maximum tempo, belongs to which coastal state?
questions.explanation: Fugdi is performed by Goan women during Dhalo, Ganesh Chaturthi, and Vrata ceremonies, building up to an exhilarating, breathless tempo.

questions.question: The 'Dhalo' is a sacred, slow-paced winter folk dance performed by women of which state across 12 moonlit nights?
questions.explanation: Dhalo is one of the oldest ritualistic group dances of Goan Hindu women, prayed for the welfare of the family and village.

questions.question: The 'Dekhni' dance of Goa is unique because it blends:
options: Western Portuguese melodies (violin, brass) with traditional Konkani themes of temple dancers (Devadasis)
questions.explanation: Dekhni is a semi-classical song-and-dance genre in Konkani depicting Devadasis crossing rivers to reach temple performances.

questions.question: Which Portuguese-influenced ballroom couple folk dance is popular among the Christian community of Goa?
questions.explanation: Corridinho is a Portuguese folk dance of the Algarve region adopted into Goan cultural celebrations, danced by couples in colorful costumes.

questions.question: The 'Gaur Maria' dance, renowned for male dancers wearing monumental bison-horn headdresses adorned with cowrie shells, belongs to which tribe of Bastar, Chhattisgarh?
questions.explanation: The Gaur Maria dance of Bastar depicts hunting the wild bison (Gaur), with men beating massive cylindrical brass drums.

questions.question: The 'Bhagoria' festival dance, where young tribal youth choose life partners, is celebrated by which tribes in Jhabua and Alirajpur, Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Bhagoria is celebrated in the haats (weekly markets) before Holi, famous for colorful turbans, flutes, and community dances.

questions.question: The 'Badhai' dance is a popular ceremonial congratulatory folk dance of which region of Madhya Pradesh, performed on weddings and births?
questions.explanation: Badhai is performed in Bundelkhand on festive occasions, accompanied by the Dholak, Timki, and metallic Manjira.

questions.question: The 'Grida' dance of Madhya Pradesh is performed by villagers during which agricultural season?
options: When the winter Rabi crops (wheat, mustard, gram) start blooming
questions.explanation: Grida dance is celebrated by agricultural communities across MP from morning to night when Rabi crops sway in the winter breeze.

questions.question: The 'Kunbi' dance of Goa is named after which indigenous agricultural community?
questions.explanation: Kunbi dance is performed by Kunbi women wearing traditional red chequered 'Dento' sarees tied with a knot at the shoulder.

questions.question: The 'Pardhauni' dance is performed by the Baiga tribe of Madhya Pradesh during:
options: Wedding celebrations to welcome the bridegroom's marriage procession (Baraat)
questions.explanation: Pardhauni is a joyful wedding dance of the Baiga tribe featuring a dummy elephant made of wood and bamboo.

dance_q4.title: SSC CGL Dance PYQ - Set 4: South India & Tribal Traditions

questions.question: The 'Yakshagana' traditional theatre-dance form, featuring towering decorated headdresses (Kirita) and vigorous footwork, belongs to which state?
questions.explanation: Yakshagana ('Song of the Celestial Beings') is a 500-year-old theatrical dance-drama of coastal Karnataka depicting epics like Ramayana and Mahabharata.

questions.question: The 'Dollu Kunitha' drum dance, where performers wear heavy drums hung around their necks and execute complex acrobatic patterns, belongs to which community of Karnataka?
questions.explanation: Dollu Kunitha is a thunderous folk drum dance of the Kuruba shepherd community in Karnataka, performed with high jumps and cymbals.

questions.question: The 'Veeragase' dance of Karnataka, performed during Dasara with wooden swords and heroic proclamations, is dedicated to which mythological warrior?
questions.explanation: Veeragase is an energetic ritual dance of the Lingayat community of Karnataka, reenacting Lord Veerabhadra destroying Daksha's sacrifice.

questions.question: The 'Kamsale' dance of Karnataka is performed by devotees of Lord Male Mahadeshwara using which unique musical prop?
options: A pair of heavy brass cymbals (Kamsale)
questions.explanation: Kamsale is an intricate martial rhythm dance of southern Karnataka where devotees strike hand-held brass cymbals in high-speed acrobatic rhythms.

questions.question: The 'Theyyam' (or Kaliyattam) sacred ritual dance-drama, where the performer is transformed into a living deity, belongs to which region of Kerala?
questions.explanation: Theyyam (derived from 'Daivam' or God) is an ancient ritual art of North Malabar where performers wear towering headdresses (Mudi) and face paint.

questions.question: The 'Padayani' (Padeni) ritual theatre dance of Kerala, performed in Bhadrakali temples, is famous for huge masks made from:
questions.explanation: Padayani dancers wear towering Kolam headgear crafted from the spathe of areca nut palms to enact the pacification of fiery Goddess Bhadrakali.

questions.question: The 'Oppana' folk dance of Kerala is traditionally performed by women of which community during wedding celebrations?
questions.explanation: Oppana is a celebratory bridal dance of Mappila women in Malabar, dancing in a circle around the bride while clapping rhythmically and singing.

questions.question: The 'Margamkali' is an ancient community round-dance and song tradition belonging to which Christian community of Kerala?
questions.explanation: Margamkali ('The Way / Path') depicts the arrival and missionary work of Saint Thomas the Apostle in Kerala in 52 CE.

questions.question: Which classical-folk satire solo dance of Kerala was created by 18th-century Malayalam poet Kunchan Nambiar as an alternative to elitist Sanskrit drama?
questions.explanation: Ottamthullal is a humorous solo dance-theatre created by Kunchan Nambiar, accompanied by the Mridangam and cymbals, delivering sharp social commentary.

questions.question: The 'Karagattam' folk dance of Tamil Nadu involves performers balancing which decorated object on their heads in honour of the rain goddess Mariamman?
options: A brass pot decorated with flowers and a wooden parrot (Karagam)
questions.explanation: Karagattam (pot dance) is performed with either Aatta Karagam (entertainment) or Sakthi Karagam (devotional) balanced gracefully on the head.

questions.question: The 'Mayil Attam' (Peacock Dance) of Tamil Nadu and Kerala is performed during Murugan temple festivals where dancers:
options: Dress in elaborate peacock feathers with an artificial beak that can open and close
questions.explanation: Mayil Attam dancers wear peacock feather costumes and talons, imitating the majestic strut, wing-spreading, and head-bobbing of Lord Murugan's mount.

questions.question: The 'Kavadi Aattam' (Burden Dance) is an arduous ceremonial sacrificial dance performed by devotees of which Hindu deity across Tamil Nadu and Malaysia?
questions.explanation: Devotees carry a decorated wooden or metallic arch (Kavadi) on their shoulders, often observing fasts and vows while walking to Murugan hill temples.

questions.question: The 'Kummi' folk dance of Tamil Nadu and Kerala is distinctive because it is performed:
options: Without any musical instruments, using only synchronized rhythmic hand-clapping and singing
questions.explanation: Kummi is one of the oldest forms of folk dancing in Tamil Nadu, where women stand in circular groups clapping hands to maintain rhythm.

questions.question: The 'Oyilattam' (Dance of Grace) of Tamil Nadu was traditionally performed by men holding what in their hands?
questions.explanation: Oyilattam is an energetic folk dance of the Kongu Nadu region of Tamil Nadu where dancers wave colored cloths and wear ankle bells.

questions.question: The 'Perini Shivatandavam' (Dance of Warriors) of Telangana was revived from 13th-century temple sculptures of which historic dynasty?
questions.explanation: Perini Shivatandavam was performed by soldiers before marching to war in the Kakatiya kingdom; revived by Natyacharya Dr. Nataraja Ramakrishna.

questions.question: The 'Dhimsa' tribal folk dance is performed by women of the Porja and Valmiki tribes in which picturesque valley of Andhra Pradesh?
questions.explanation: Dhimsa is a community circle dance of the Araku Valley performed during weddings and harvest festivals to establish tribal camaraderie.

questions.question: The 'Bonalu' festival in Hyderabad and Telangana features the energetic dance of 'Pothuraju', who is considered the:
options: Fierce whip-wielding brother and protector of the seven goddess sisters (Goddess Mahankali)
questions.explanation: Pothuraju wears a red dhoti, smears turmeric and vermilion on his body, carries a heavy whip, and dances furiously ahead of the Bonalu procession.

questions.question: The 'Lambadi' (or Banjara) dance of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka is famous for female dancers wearing:
options: Vibrant, heavy dresses embroidered with intricate mirror-work, beads, cowrie shells, and heavy ivory bangles
questions.explanation: Lambadi dance is performed by women of the nomadic Banjara community, singing songs of daily life and pastoral migrations.

questions.question: The 'Garadi' folk dance, performed with iron rods and shields where dancers wear giant masks of monkey soldiers (Vanaras), belongs to which Union Territory?
questions.explanation: Garadi is an ancient victory dance of Puducherry celebrating Lord Rama's vanquishing of Ravana with the Vanara army.

questions.question: Which folk dance of the Lakshadweep islands is performed by men holding colorful wooden swords and shields to the beats of folk drums?
questions.explanation: Parichakali (shield dance) and Kolkali (stick dance) are traditional martial folk arts of the Minicoy and Lakshadweep islands.

questions.question: The 'Lava' dance is a popular, colorful folk dance performed by the Maldive-origin people of which island of Lakshadweep?
questions.explanation: Lava dance is performed by men of Minicoy Island dressed in red trousers, white sash, and headscarves, dancing to the beating of the Dhol.

questions.question: The 'Silambattam' of Tamil Nadu is primarily recognized as:
options: An ancient weapon-based martial art using a long bamboo staff (Silambam)
questions.explanation: Silambam is an ancient Dravidian martial art using a 5-foot bamboo cane, with intricate footwork patterns categorized under martial dances.

questions.question: The 'Kalaripayattu' of Kerala, considered one of the oldest fighting arts in the world, was founded according to legend by which sage?
questions.explanation: Legend credits Sage Parashurama with establishing the northern style (Vadakan) of Kalaripayattu, featuring weapons like the Urumi (flexible sword).

questions.question: The 'Bhoota Kola' is an ancient ritualistic spirit-worship dance ceremony performed in the Tulu Nadu region of which state?
questions.explanation: Bhoota Kola is a spirit possession ritual and dance of Tulu Nadu (depicted famously in the film 'Kantara') in honor of local protector spirits (Daivas).

questions.question: The 'Kaniyan Koothu' is a ritualistic exorcism and folk dance tradition of southern Tamil Nadu performed by the Kaniyan community wearing:
options: Male performers dressed in female attire playing the Magudam (frame drum)
questions.explanation: Kaniyan Koothu is an ancient folk ritual performed in Sudalai Madan and Amman temples of Tirunelveli and Thoothukudi.

dance_q5.title: SSC CGL Dance PYQ - Set 5: 8 Classical Dances & Repertoire

questions.question: How many classical dance forms are officially recognized by the Sangeet Natak Akademi (SNA) of India?
