festivals_q6.title: SSC CGL Festival PYQ - Set 6: 2021-2024 Exam PYQs

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Hornbill Festival' of Nagaland is celebrated in which month of the year?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is celebrated every year from December 1 to December 10 at Kisama Heritage Village, coinciding with Nagaland Statehood Day (December 1).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Chapchar Kut' is a festival of which northeastern state?
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is the greatest festival of Mizoram, celebrated in spring after the jhum operations (bamboo clearing) are over.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Bathukamma' is a floral festival celebrated predominantly in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bathukamma is celebrated by the women of Telangana during the nine days of Durga Navratri, ending on Durgashtami as 'Saddula Bathukamma'.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Wangala Festival' is celebrated by which tribal community?
questions.explanation: The Wangala Festival is the post-harvest festival of the Garo people of Meghalaya and Assam, celebrating the Sun God Saljong.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: In which state is the ancient religious fair 'Ambubachi Mela' held annually in June?
questions.explanation: Ambubachi Mela is an annual Hindu mela held at Kamakhya Temple in Guwahati, celebrating the earth's fertility during the monsoon.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Losoong' (Namsoong) festival marks the start of the New Year in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Losoong is celebrated in Sikkim in December, marking the end of the harvest season and the beginning of the Bhutia and Lepcha New Year.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Ugadi' is celebrated as the New Year in which month of the Hindu calendar?
questions.explanation: Ugadi is celebrated on the first day of the bright half of Chaitra month, heralding the arrival of spring and the Deccan New Year.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Nuakhai' is an agricultural festival mainly observed by the people of which state?
questions.explanation: Nuakhai is the agricultural festival of Western Odisha observed to welcome the new season's rice crop on the day after Ganesh Chaturthi.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: 'Medaram Jathara' is celebrated in which state to commemorate the tribal revolt against Kakatiya rulers?
questions.explanation: Medaram Jathara commemorates the battle of mother-daughter warriors Sammakka and Sarakka against Kakatiya rulers imposing taxes during a severe drought.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: The festival of 'Onam' is associated with the return of which mythological king to Kerala?
questions.explanation: Legend says Lord Vishnu in his Vamana avatar granted King Mahabali the boon to visit his beloved subjects once every year on Thiru Onam day.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Baisakhi' festival marks the founding of the Khalsa Panth in which year by Guru Gobind Singh?
questions.explanation: Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth at Anandpur Sahib on Baisakhi day in 1699, bestowing the Five K's (Kesh, Kangha, Kara, Kachhera, Kirpan).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: In which city is the famous 'Surajkund International Crafts Mela' organized every year?
questions.explanation: Surajkund Crafts Mela is held in Faridabad, attracting international artisans, folklorists, and tourists to promote rural crafts.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Kharchi Puja' is a Hindu festival celebrated in which state featuring 14 deities?
questions.explanation: Kharchi Puja is performed in Old Agartala in Tripura in July, where 14 royal family deities (Chaturdasha Devata) are carried to the Howrah river for ceremonial baths.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Tarnetar Fair' is held in which state of India?
questions.explanation: Tarnetar Fair is celebrated around the Trinetreshwar temple in Surendranagar district of Gujarat, famous for colorful embroidered umbrellas.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: 'Gudi Padwa' is celebrated in Maharashtra on the first day of which Hindu month?
questions.explanation: Gudi Padwa marks the beginning of the New Year according to the Luni-Solar Hindu calendar, falling on Chaitra Shukla Pratipada.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Kumbh Mela' is held at four places in India. Which of the following is NOT one of those places?
options: Varanasi (Kumbh is held at Prayagraj, Haridwar, Ujjain, and Nashik)
questions.explanation: Varanasi does NOT host a Kumbh Mela. The four sacred locations are Prayagraj (Sangam), Haridwar (Ganga), Ujjain (Shipra), and Nashik (Godavari).

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: The festival of 'Chhath Puja' is dedicated to the worship of which celestial body?
questions.explanation: Chhath Puja is dedicated to the solar deity Surya and Chhathi Maiya, thanking them for sustaining life on Earth and granting boons.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Sekrenyi' festival is celebrated by which tribe of Nagaland in February?
questions.explanation: Sekrenyi is the annual 10-day purification festival of the Angami Nagas, celebrating renewed vitality and warding off misfortune.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: 'Sonpur Cattle Fair' is held at the confluence of which two rivers in Bihar?
questions.explanation: The historic Sonpur Cattle Fair is located at Harihar Kshetra on the confluence of the sacred rivers Ganga and Gandak in Bihar.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Yaoshang' festival in Manipur is celebrated for five days on the full moon day of which month?
questions.explanation: Yaoshang begins on the full moon day of Phalguna (February/March) and is the premier cultural festival of the Meitei community.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2021: 'Ali-Ai-Ligang' is a spring festival associated with which agricultural activity in Assam?
options: Seed sowing (onset of Ahu paddy cultivation)
questions.explanation: Ali-Ai-Ligang is the spring festival of the Mishing tribe of Assam, marking the beginning of seed sowing on the first Wednesday of Phalguna.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Pushkar Fair' is held on the banks of Pushkar Lake in Rajasthan on which auspicious tithi?
questions.explanation: The Pushkar Camel Fair culminates on Kartik Purnima when thousands of pilgrims take a holy dip in Pushkar Lake.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2022: Which state celebrates the festival 'Garia Puja' by sacrificing roosters and offering rice beer to God Garia?
questions.explanation: Garia Puja is a seven-day community festival celebrated by the indigenous Tripuri and Jamatia tribes of Tripura in April.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2024: 'Behdienkhlam' festival is celebrated annually in July by which tribe of Meghalaya?
questions.explanation: Behdienkhlam is celebrated by the Pnars in Jaintia Hills to seek divine blessings for bumper crops and to ward off the demon of plague.

questions.question: In SSC CGL 2023: 'Kolkata Durga Puja' was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in which year?
questions.explanation: Kolkata's Durga Puja was officially inscribed by UNESCO on its Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity list in December 2021 during the 16th committee session.

polity_q1.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 1: Parliament vs State Confusing Articles

questions.question: Which pair of Articles correctly represents the Ordinance-making power of the President of India and the Governor of a State respectively?
questions.explanation: Article 123 empowers the President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament; similarly, Article 213 empowers the Governor during recess of the State Legislature. Both ordinances have the same force as an Act but must be approved within 6 weeks of reassembly.

questions.question: Under which Article is the Annual Financial Statement (Budget) presented to the Union Parliament and State Legislature respectively?
questions.explanation: The Constitution does not use the word 'Budget'; it refers to it as 'Annual Financial Statement' under Article 112 for the Union and Article 202 for the States.

questions.question: What constitutes a 'Money Bill' is defined under which Article for Parliament and State Legislatures respectively?
questions.explanation: Article 110 defines Money Bills for the Union (solely certified by the Lok Sabha Speaker). Article 199 defines Money Bills for State Legislatures (certified by the Legislative Assembly Speaker).

questions.question: What is the special procedure regarding Money Bills under Article 109 (Union) and Article 198 (State)?
options: Money Bills CANNOT be introduced in the Upper House (Rajya Sabha / Legislative Council) and the Upper House must return them within 14 days
They can be introduced in either House
questions.explanation: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Lower House upon recommendation of the President/Governor. The Upper House can only make recommendations within 14 days; it cannot reject or amend it.

questions.question: Under which Article does the Governor of a State have the power to reserve a Bill passed by the State Legislature for the consideration of the President?
questions.explanation: Under Article 200, the Governor can grant assent, withhold assent, return the bill for reconsideration, or reserve it for the President's consideration (mandatory if the bill endangers the High Court's position).

questions.question: When a State Bill is reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President under Article 201, what is the constitutional position of the President?
options: The President can give assent, withhold assent, or direct the Governor to return it; if passed again by the State Legislature, the President is NOT bound to give assent
President is bound to give assent within 14 days
questions.explanation: Unlike an ordinary Union Bill under Article 111 where the President is bound to give assent if passed again, the President is NOT bound to give assent to a reconsidered State Bill under Article 201.

questions.question: While Article 74 mandates that the President 'shall act' in accordance with the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, what unique power does the Governor enjoy under Article 163?
options: The Governor has explicit constitutional discretionary powers where the Governor's decision taken in his discretion is final and cannot be questioned
Governor acts only on Prime Minister's orders
Governor is bound by Chief Minister's advice in all matters
questions.explanation: Article 163(1) contains the phrase 'except in so far as he is by or under this Constitution required to exercise his functions in his discretion', giving the Governor constitutional discretion (unlike the President).

questions.question: Which pair of Articles provides for the appointment of the Attorney General for India and the Advocate General for the State respectively?
questions.explanation: Article 76 establishes the Attorney General for India (appointed by the President, holds office during pleasure). Article 165 establishes the Advocate General for each State (appointed by the Governor, holds office during pleasure).

questions.question: Under Article 88 and Article 177, what special right do Ministers and the Attorney General / Advocate General enjoy?
options: The right to speak in and participate in proceedings of either House and any committee, but WITHOUT the right to vote
Full voting rights in both Houses
questions.explanation: Article 88 (Union) and Article 177 (State) grant the right of audience and speech in both legislative chambers, but explicitly deny the right to vote unless they are an elected member of that specific House.

questions.question: Under which Article can the Parliament of India create or abolish a Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) in a State?
questions.explanation: Article 169 provides that Parliament may by law abolish or create a Legislative Council if the State Legislative Assembly passes a resolution by a Special Majority (majority of total membership and not less than 2/3rd of members present and voting).

questions.question: Is a law passed by Parliament under Article 169 for the creation or abolition of a State Legislative Council considered an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368?
options: No, it is passed by a Simple Majority in Parliament and is not deemed an amendment under Article 368
Yes, requires special majority of Parliament
questions.explanation: Article 169(3) specifically states that no such law enacted by Parliament shall be deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.

questions.question: How many States in India currently have a bicameral legislature (possessing both a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council)?
options: 6 States (Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh)
questions.explanation: Currently, only 6 states have a Vidhan Parishad: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana, and Uttar Pradesh (remembered by the acronym KUMBAT).

questions.question: What is the maximum and minimum strength of a State Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) under Article 170?
options: Maximum 500 members and Minimum 60 members (subject to exceptions for Goa, Mizoram, Sikkim)
questions.explanation: Article 170 mandates between 60 and 500 members. Exceptions exist for smaller states: Sikkim (32), Goa (40), Mizoram (40), and Puducherry UT (30).

questions.question: What is the maximum and minimum permissible strength of a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) under Article 171?
options: Maximum one-third of the total strength of the Legislative Assembly, and minimum 40 members
questions.explanation: Article 171(1) stipulates that the total membership of the Legislative Council shall not exceed one-third of the Legislative Assembly, and cannot be less than 40.

questions.question: What is the minimum age prescribed for membership of the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha respectively under Article 84?
questions.explanation: Under Article 84: Lok Sabha is minimum 25 years, Rajya Sabha is minimum 30 years. Similarly, under Article 173: Vidhan Sabha is 25 years, Vidhan Parishad is 30 years.

questions.question: What is the minimum age required to contest for the office of President of India, Vice-President, and Governor of a State?
options: 35 years for all three (President Art 58, VP Art 66, Governor Art 157)
questions.explanation: To be eligible for election as President, Vice-President, or Governor, a citizen must have completed the age of 35 years.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to be elected as a member of a Gram Panchayat or Municipality?
questions.explanation: While the voting age is 18 years, the minimum age required to contest elections to local bodies (Panchayats and Municipalities) is 21 years.

questions.question: Under which Articles are the disqualifications for membership of Parliament and State Legislatures laid down?
questions.explanation: Article 102 and Article 191 specify disqualifications: holding an office of profit, unsound mind, undischarged insolvent, non-citizenship, or disqualified under the Tenth Schedule.

questions.question: Who decides questions on the disqualification of a Member of Parliament under Article 103 (other than Tenth Schedule anti-defection)?
options: The President of India, whose decision is final, but after obtaining the opinion of the Election Commission of India (ECI)
questions.explanation: Under Article 103, the President decides disqualification matters after obtaining and acting in accordance with the binding opinion of the Election Commission of India.

questions.question: Who decides questions on disqualification of a member of a State Legislature under Article 192 (other than Tenth Schedule)?
options: The Governor of the State, acting in accordance with the opinion of the Election Commission of India
questions.explanation: Under Article 192, the Governor refers the question to the Election Commission of India and acts according to its binding opinion.

questions.question: Under which Articles are the parliamentary privileges of Parliament and State Legislatures governed?
questions.explanation: Article 105 defines the powers, privileges, and immunities of Parliament and its members (freedom of speech in Parliament, immunity from court proceedings for votes/speeches). Article 194 defines identical privileges for State Legislatures.

questions.question: Can a Joint Sitting of both Houses be summoned for a deadlocked Bill in a State Legislature having a bicameral setup?
options: NO, there is NO provision for a Joint Sitting in State Legislatures under the Constitution
questions.explanation: A major trap in SSC exams: Article 108 provides for a Joint Sitting of Parliament for the Union, but there is NO constitutional provision for a Joint Sitting in State Legislatures! The Legislative Assembly's will ultimately prevails.

questions.question: What is the maximum duration for which a State Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad) can delay an Ordinary Bill passed by the Legislative Assembly?
options: Maximum 4 months in total (3 months in the first instance, and 1 month in the second instance)
questions.explanation: Under Article 197, the Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for 3 months initially. If passed again by the Assembly, the Council can delay it for only 1 month, after which the bill is deemed passed.

questions.question: Who presides over a Joint Sitting of Parliament summoned by the President under Article 108?
options: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha (or in his absence, the Deputy Speaker; if absent, Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha)
The Chairman of Rajya Sabha (Vice President)
questions.explanation: The Vice-President (Chairman of Rajya Sabha) NEVER presides over a Joint Sitting because he is not an elected member of Parliament! It is presided over by the Speaker of Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Under which Article does the President summon, prorogue, and dissolve the Lok Sabha?
options: Article 85 (for Parliament) and Article 174 (for State Legislature by Governor)
questions.explanation: Article 85 governs sessions, prorogation, and dissolution of Parliament. Article 174 governs sessions, prorogation, and dissolution of State Legislatures.

polity_q2.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 2: Parts, Schedules & 22 Languages

questions.question: How many Parts, Articles, and Schedules were there in the original Constitution of India when adopted on November 26, 1949?
questions.explanation: The original Constitution consisted of a Preamble, 395 Articles divided into 22 Parts, and 8 Schedules. Currently, it has 25 Parts and 12 Schedules through amendments.

questions.question: Which Part of the Indian Constitution was repealed/deleted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956?
options: Part VII (The States in Part B of the First Schedule)
questions.explanation: Part VII (Article 238), which dealt with the erstwhile Part B princely states, was omitted by the States Reorganisation 7th Amendment Act, 1956.

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution deals with 'The Union Territories' (Articles 239 to 242)?
questions.explanation: Part VIII governs Union Territories, including Article 239AA which contains special provisions with respect to Delhi (National Capital Territory).

questions.question: Part IX, Part IX-A, and Part IX-B of the Constitution govern which institutions respectively?
options: Panchayats (Part IX), Municipalities (Part IX-A), and Co-operative Societies (Part IX-B)
Union Territories, Scheduled Areas, and States
questions.explanation: Part IX was inserted by 73rd Amendment 1992, Part IX-A by 74th Amendment 1992, and Part IX-B by 97th Amendment 2011.

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution deals with 'Tribunals' (Articles 323A and 323B), inserted by the 42nd Amendment Act 1976?
questions.explanation: Part XIV-A was added upon the recommendations of the Swaran Singh Committee to set up Administrative Tribunals (CAT and SAT).

questions.question: Which Part of the Constitution deals with 'Elections' (Articles 324 to 329)?
questions.explanation: Part XV governs the superintendence, direction, and control of elections vested in the Election Commission under Article 324.

questions.question: Part XVII of the Constitution (Articles 343 to 351) deals with:
questions.explanation: Part XVII governs Official Language: Chapter I (Language of the Union - Hindi in Devanagari script, Art 343), Chapter II (Regional languages), Chapter III (Supreme Court & High Courts), and Chapter IV (Directives for Hindi development, Art 351).

questions.question: Part XVIII of the Constitution (Articles 352 to 360) deals with which extraordinary mechanism?
options: Emergency Provisions (National, State, and Financial Emergencies)
questions.explanation: Part XVIII contains the three types of emergencies: National Emergency (Art 352), President's Rule (Art 356), and Financial Emergency (Art 360).

questions.question: Article 368, which deals with the power of Parliament to amend the Constitution and procedure therefor, is the sole Article in which Part?
questions.explanation: Part XX contains only one single Article—Article 368—governing constitutional amendment procedures.

questions.question: Special provisions for states like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Sikkim, and Karnataka (Articles 371 to 371-J) are in which Part?
options: Part XXI (Temporary, Transitional and Special Provisions)
questions.explanation: Part XXI contains Articles 369 to 392, including Article 370 (abrogated in 2019) and Article 371 to 371-J providing asymmetric federal autonomy to specific states.

questions.question: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the salaries, allowances, and emoluments of the President, Governors, Speaker, Judges, and the CAG?
questions.explanation: The Second Schedule details salaries of constitutional dignitaries. (Note: The Prime Minister and Union Ministers are NOT mentioned in the Second Schedule!).

questions.question: Whose oaths of office are notably EXCLUDED from the Third Schedule (Forms of Oaths or Affirmations) of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Third Schedule contains oaths for Ministers, MPs, Judges, and the CAG. However, the oaths for the President (Article 60), Vice-President (Article 69), and Governor (Article 159) are specified directly within their constitutional articles.

questions.question: The Fourth Schedule to the Constitution of India deals with:
options: Allocation of seats in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha) to States and Union Territories
questions.explanation: The Fourth Schedule details Rajya Sabha seat distribution based on population. Uttar Pradesh has the highest allocation (31 seats).

questions.question: The Sixth Schedule of the Indian Constitution provides for the administration of tribal areas in which four Northeastern States exclusively?
options: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram (Remember: AMTM)
Arunachal Pradesh, Nagaland, Manipur, and Mizoram
questions.explanation: The Sixth Schedule applies exclusively to tribal areas in 4 states: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram. (Manipur and Nagaland are NOT covered by the Sixth Schedule!).

questions.question: What autonomous administrative bodies are created under the Sixth Schedule in the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura, and Mizoram?
options: Autonomous District Councils (ADCs) and Regional Councils
questions.explanation: ADCs have legislative, judicial, and taxation powers, operating with up to 30 members (26 elected, 4 nominated by the Governor).

questions.question: The Fifth Schedule of the Constitution applies to the administration and control of Scheduled Areas and Scheduled Tribes in:
options: 10 States other than the four Sixth Schedule States (Andhra, Telangana, Odisha, Jharkhand, MP, CG, Rajasthan, Gujarat, Maharashtra, HP)
questions.explanation: The Fifth Schedule covers tribal areas in 10 states where Tribes Advisory Councils (TAC) consisting of up to 20 members advise the Governor.

questions.question: The Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India (Article 246) divides legislative subjects into three lists. What are their current item counts?
options: Union List (100 items), State List (61 items), and Concurrent List (52 items)
questions.explanation: Originally 97 (Union), 66 (State), and 47 (Concurrent). After transfers by the 42nd Amendment, they stand at 100, 61, and 52 subjects respectively.

questions.question: Five subjects—Education, Forests, Weights & Measures, Protection of Wild Animals & Birds, and Administration of Justice—were shifted from the State List to the Concurrent List by which Amendment?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment 1976 transferred five critical subjects from the State List to the Concurrent List to enable central policy intervention.

questions.question: Where do 'Residuary Powers' of legislation (subjects not mentioned in any of the three lists of the Seventh Schedule) lie in India under Article 248?
questions.explanation: Unlike the USA where residuary powers belong to the states, Article 248 vests all residuary legislative authority exclusively in the Parliament of India (modelled on Canada).

questions.question: How many official languages were originally recognized in the Eighth Schedule, and how many are there currently?
questions.explanation: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages. Sindhi was added by 21st Amendment (1967); Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali by 71st Amendment (1992); Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali by 92nd Amendment (2003).

questions.question: Which language was added to the Eighth Schedule by the 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967?
questions.explanation: Sindhi was the 15th language added to the Eighth Schedule via the 21st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1967.

questions.question: Which three languages were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 71st Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992?
questions.explanation: The 71st Amendment added Konkani, Manipuri (Meitei), and Nepali in 1992.

questions.question: Which four languages were added to the Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003?
options: Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali (Remember: BDMS)
questions.explanation: The 92nd Amendment (effective 2004) added Bodo, Dogri, Maithili, and Santhali, raising the total count to 22.

questions.question: Which of the following widely spoken languages is NOT included in the Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: Neither English nor Bhojpuri is included in the Eighth Schedule. (English is the authoritative language for courts/laws under Art 348, but not in Schedule 8).

questions.question: The Tenth Schedule (Anti-Defection Law) was added to the Constitution by which Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 52nd Amendment 1985 inserted the Tenth Schedule during Rajiv Gandhi's tenure, setting grounds for disqualification due to voluntary party defection or defying a party whip.

polity_q3.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 3: Fundamental Rights, Writs & DPSP

questions.question: What is the definition of 'State' under Article 12 of the Indian Constitution for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights?
options: Government and Parliament of India, Government and Legislature of each State, all local authorities, and other authorities within India
questions.explanation: Article 12 defines 'State' broadly to include the Union, States, local bodies (municipalities, panchayats), and statutory/public corporations like LIC, ONGC, and SBI.

questions.question: Is the Judiciary included within the definition of 'State' under Article 12 when delivering judicial judgments?
options: NO, the judiciary while performing judicial functions is not included in 'State' (Naresh Shridhar Mirajkar case)
questions.explanation: Judicial decisions of courts cannot be challenged as violations of fundamental rights under Article 12; however, administrative acts of the judiciary fall under 'State'.

questions.question: What does Article 13(2) of the Constitution declare regarding laws that abridge Fundamental Rights?
options: The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges fundamental rights; any such law shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void
Such laws are valid for 6 months
Such laws are referred to the Governor
questions.explanation: Article 13 is the foundation of Judicial Review in India, establishing the Doctrine of Severability and Doctrine of Eclipse for unconstitutional laws.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Right was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'heart and soul of the Constitution' without which the Constitution would be a nullity?
questions.explanation: Article 32 guarantees the right to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Ambedkar declared it the most important Article of the Constitution.

questions.question: What is the crucial difference between the writ jurisdiction of the Supreme Court (Article 32) and the High Courts (Article 226)?
options: High Court writ jurisdiction under Article 226 is WIDER than Supreme Court under Article 32 because High Courts can issue writs for fundamental rights AND for 'any other legal purpose'
questions.explanation: Under Article 32, the Supreme Court can issue writs ONLY for Fundamental Rights; under Article 226, High Courts can issue writs for Fundamental Rights as well as ordinary legal and statutory rights.

questions.question: Is the right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 itself a Fundamental Right?
options: YES, Article 32 is itself a Fundamental Right in Part III, whereas Article 226 is a constitutional right but not in Part III
No, it is only a procedural right
questions.explanation: Because Article 32 is in Part III, the Supreme Court cannot refuse to hear a fundamental rights petition. High Court jurisdiction under Art 226 is discretionary.

questions.question: Which writ is known as the 'Bulwark of Individual Liberty' against arbitrary and illegal detention?
options: Habeas Corpus ('You shall have the body')
questions.explanation: Habeas Corpus can be issued against both public authorities and private individuals to test the legal justification of detention.

questions.question: Against whom can the writ of 'Mandamus' NOT be issued according to constitutional law?
options: Against the President of India or State Governors, private individuals, or for enforcing non-statutory contracts
questions.explanation: Under Article 361, Mandamus cannot lie against the President or Governor for the exercise of their powers, nor can it compel discretionary duties.

questions.question: What is the distinction between the writ of 'Prohibition' and the writ of 'Certiorari'?
options: Prohibition is preventive (issued during trial to stop lower court from exceeding jurisdiction); Certiorari is curative (issued after order to quash illegal decision)
Certiorari is only for private bodies
questions.explanation: Prohibition halts ongoing proceedings in an inferior court/tribunal lacking jurisdiction. Certiorari quashes an order already passed without jurisdiction or in violation of natural justice.

questions.question: Which writ can be sought by any public-spirited citizen without having personal interest or direct standing in the matter (Relaxation of Locus Standi)?
questions.explanation: In Quo-Warranto, any citizen can challenge the usurper of a substantive public office created by statute or Constitution, even if the petitioner is not personally injured.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Rights are available exclusively to Indian citizens and DENIED to foreigners/aliens?
questions.explanation: Articles 15 (non-discrimination), 16 (public employment), 19 (six freedoms), 29 (minority interests), and 30 (educational institutions) are reserved exclusively for Indian citizens.

questions.question: Which Fundamental Rights CANNOT be suspended even during a National Emergency proclaimed under Article 352?
options: Articles 20 (protection in respect of conviction) and 21 (right to life and personal liberty)
questions.explanation: The 44th Constitutional Amendment Act 1978 amended Article 359 to guarantee that the enforcement of Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended during any emergency.

questions.question: Article 19's six democratic freedoms are automatically suspended ONLY when a National Emergency is declared on which specific grounds?
options: War or External Aggression (External Emergency), NOT on Armed Rebellion
questions.explanation: Under Article 358 (amended by 44th Amendment), Article 19 is automatically suspended only during an External Emergency (war/aggression), never during an Armed Rebellion.

questions.question: What was the phrase 'Internal Disturbance' in Article 352 replaced with by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978?
questions.explanation: To prevent misuse as occurred in 1975, the 44th Amendment substituted 'armed rebellion' for the subjective term 'internal disturbance'.

questions.question: The 'Right to Education' was inserted into Part III as Article 21-A by which landmark Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 86th Amendment 2002 made free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years, added Article 21A, modified Article 45, and added Fundamental Duty 51A(k).

questions.question: Which Supreme Court judgment first recognized the Right to Education as flowing from the Right to Life under Article 21 in 1993?
options: Unni Krishnan v. State of Andhra Pradesh
Mohini Jain v. State of Karnataka
questions.explanation: In Unni Krishnan (1993), the Supreme Court ruled that the right to education up to age 14 is a concomitant fundamental right under Article 21.

questions.question: What does Article 20(2) of the Indian Constitution prohibit?
options: Double Jeopardy (No person shall be prosecuted and punished for the same offence more than once)
questions.explanation: Article 20(2) incorporates the doctrine of Double Jeopardy (Autrefois convict), protecting citizens against multiple prosecutions for the same crime before judicial courts.

questions.question: What does Article 20(3) of the Constitution guarantee?
options: Protection against Self-Incrimination ('No person accused of any offence shall be compelled to be a witness against himself')
questions.explanation: Article 20(3) guarantees immunity against self-incrimination, which applies exclusively to a person formally accused of an offence.

questions.question: What is the maximum period a person can be detained under a preventive detention law without obtaining the opinion of an Advisory Board under Article 22?
options: Three months (reduced to two months by 44th Amendment, but yet to be notified; hence 3 months holds)
questions.explanation: Article 22(4) mandates that preventive detention beyond 3 months requires approval from an Advisory Board chaired by High Court judges.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) contained in Part IV (Articles 36 to 51) are borrowed from which country's constitution?
questions.explanation: The concept of DPSP was borrowed from the Irish Constitution (which had copied it from the Spanish Constitution).

questions.question: Are the Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) enforceable in courts of law under Article 37?
options: NO, Article 37 explicitly declares DPSPs non-justiciable, but fundamental in the governance of the country
questions.explanation: Article 37 explicitly states that DPSPs shall not be enforceable by any court, but it shall be the duty of the State to apply these principles in making laws.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to secure a Uniform Civil Code (UCC) for the citizens throughout India?
questions.explanation: Article 44 in Part IV directs: 'The State shall endeavour to secure for the citizens a uniform civil code throughout the territory of India.'

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to organize Village Panchayats as units of self-government (Gandhian Principle)?
questions.explanation: Article 40 fulfills Mahatma Gandhi's vision of Gram Swaraj, directing the state to endow village panchayats with powers to function as self-governing units.

questions.question: Which Article directs the State to separate the Judiciary from the Executive in the public services of the State?
questions.explanation: Article 50 directs the state to decouple judicial magistrate functions from executive magistrates to safeguard judicial independence.

questions.question: Which Article directs the State to promote international peace and security, maintain just relations between nations, and encourage arbitration?
questions.explanation: Article 51 forms the foundational constitutional basis of India's non-aligned and peaceful foreign policy.

polity_q4.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 4: Judiciary & Emergency Traps

questions.question: Under which Article is the Supreme Court of India declared a 'Court of Record' having the power to punish for contempt of itself?
questions.explanation: Article 129 declares the Supreme Court a Court of Record. Its records have evidentiary value and cannot be questioned in court, and it holds summary power to punish for contempt.

questions.question: Under which Article does the Supreme Court have the power to grant 'Special Leave to Appeal' (SLP) against any judgment or order in any matter?
questions.explanation: Article 136 confers extraordinary discretionary appellate power on the Supreme Court to grant special leave to appeal against any court or tribunal (except military tribunals).

questions.question: Under Article 143, the President of India may seek the advisory opinion of the Supreme Court on questions of law or public importance. What is the nature of this opinion?
options: The opinion is purely advisory and is NOT binding on the President
questions.explanation: Under Article 143 (Advisory Jurisdiction), the Supreme Court's opinion is non-binding advice. The Court may also refuse to answer non-pre-constitutional references.

questions.question: Article 142 of the Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to:
options: Pass any decree or order necessary for doing 'complete justice' in any cause or matter pending before it
questions.explanation: Article 142 provides unique plenary powers to do complete justice where statutory law is silent or inadequate (e.g. Union Carbide, Ayodhya, Chandigarh mayoral case).

questions.question: What is the sanctioned judge strength of the Supreme Court of India (including the Chief Justice of India)?
questions.explanation: Parliament increased the strength from 31 to 34 judges via the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019.

questions.question: Under which Article can a Judge of the Supreme Court or High Court be removed from office by the President on grounds of 'proved misbehaviour or incapacity'?
options: Article 124(4) for Supreme Court and Article 217(1)(b) for High Court
questions.explanation: Removal requires an address by each House of Parliament supported by a special majority (majority of total membership and not less than 2/3 of members present and voting) under the Judges (Inquiry) Act 1968.

questions.question: Has any Judge of the Supreme Court of India ever been successfully removed (impeached) from office since independence?
options: NO, no judge of the Supreme Court or High Court has ever been removed by Parliament
questions.explanation: While removal proceedings were initiated against Justice V. Ramaswami (1993) and Soumitra Sen (2011), no judge has ever been successfully impeached; motions either failed in Parliament or judges resigned before completion.

questions.question: What is the procedure for proclamation of a National Emergency under Article 352?
options: The President can issue it ONLY on the written recommendation of the Union Cabinet (not Prime Minister alone), approved by both Houses within 1 month by a Special Majority
Simple majority of Lok Sabha only
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment inserted the requirement of a written Cabinet decision to prevent solitary declarations, and reduced approval time from 2 months to 1 month by Special Majority.

questions.question: Once approved by Parliament, for how long does a National Emergency under Article 352 remain in force before requiring re-approval?
options: 6 months at a time (can be extended indefinitely with 6-month parliamentary approvals)
questions.explanation: A National Emergency can continue indefinitely, provided it is renewed by Parliament every six months with a special majority.

questions.question: What is the maximum period for which 'President's Rule' (State Emergency under Article 356) can be extended in a State under normal circumstances?
options: Maximum 3 years (approved every 6 months by simple majority)
questions.explanation: President's Rule cannot ordinarily exceed 1 year, unless a National Emergency is in operation and the Election Commission certifies that assembly elections cannot be held, subject to an outside cap of 3 years.

questions.question: Under which Article can President's Rule be imposed if a State Government fails to comply with or give effect to executive directions given by the Union?
questions.explanation: Article 365 states that failure to comply with Union directions is deemed a failure of constitutional machinery, allowing Article 356 to be invoked.

questions.question: Has a 'Financial Emergency' under Article 360 ever been declared in India?
options: NO, Financial Emergency has NEVER been declared in India so far
questions.explanation: Despite acute economic balance-of-payments crisis in 1991, Article 360 has never been invoked in the history of the Republic of India.

questions.question: What power does the Union Executive acquire during a Financial Emergency under Article 360?
options: Power to direct reduction of salaries and allowances of all or any class of persons serving the Union/State, including Judges of Supreme Court and High Courts
questions.explanation: Under Article 360(4)(b), salaries of Supreme Court and High Court judges can be reduced during a Financial Emergency.

questions.question: The 'Collegium System' for appointment and transfer of judges in higher judiciary was established through which historic Supreme Court cases?
options: Three Judges Cases: First (1981), Second (1993), and Third (1998) Judges Cases
questions.explanation: The Second Judges Case (1993) created the Collegium, and the Third Judges Case (1998) expanded it to CJI + 4 senior-most judges for SC, and CJI + 2 judges for HC.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act sought to replace the Collegium System with the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), which was struck down as unconstitutional by the Supreme Court in 2015?
questions.explanation: In the Fourth Judges Case (2015), a 5-judge bench struck down the 99th Amendment and NJAC Act, ruling that judicial primacy is an unalterable part of the Basic Structure.

questions.question: Under Article 72, the President can pardon sentences. How does the Governor's pardoning power under Article 161 differ from the President?
options: The Governor CANNOT pardon death sentences (only President can pardon death sentences), nor pardon court-martial sentences
questions.explanation: Under Article 161, a Governor cannot pardon a death sentence (though he can suspend, remit, or commute it). Only the President under Article 72 can fully grant a pardon for death.

questions.question: The electoral college for electing the President of India under Article 54 consists of:
options: Elected members of both Houses of Parliament AND elected members of State Legislative Assemblies (including Delhi and Puducherry)
Members of Parliament and Legislative Councils
questions.explanation: Nominated members of Parliament and members of State Legislative Councils (Vidhan Parishad) do NOT vote in presidential elections. Only elected MPs and elected MLAs vote.

questions.question: The electoral college for electing the Vice-President of India under Article 66 consists of:
options: ALL members (both elected AND nominated) of BOTH Houses of Parliament (Lok Sabha & Rajya Sabha) only
questions.explanation: Unlike the presidential election, state MLAs do not participate, but nominated MPs of Rajya Sabha and Lok Sabha do vote in the Vice-Presidential election.

questions.question: What method of voting is used for the election of both the President and Vice-President of India?
options: Proportional Representation by means of Single Transferable Vote (PR-STV) through secret ballot
questions.explanation: Articles 55 and 66 prescribe Proportional Representation by means of a Single Transferable Vote through secret ballot, where voters mark preferences.

questions.question: All doubts and disputes arising out of the election of a President or Vice-President of India are inquired into and decided exclusively by which authority under Article 71?
options: The Supreme Court of India, whose decision is final
questions.explanation: Under Article 71, the Supreme Court has exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate presidential and vice-presidential election petitions.

questions.question: Under Article 61, a motion for the impeachment of the President of India can be initiated in:
options: Either House of Parliament (Lok Sabha or Rajya Sabha)
questions.explanation: Impeachment charges can be initiated in either House on the sole constitutional ground of 'Violation of the Constitution', signed by 1/4th members and passed by a 2/3rd majority of the total membership.

questions.question: Under Article 67(b), the resolution for the removal of the Vice-President of India can be initiated in:
options: ONLY in the Council of States (Rajya Sabha)
questions.explanation: A resolution to remove the Vice-President can only originate in Rajya Sabha, passed by an effective majority (majority of all the then members) and agreed to by Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Who discharges the functions of the President of India when both the President and Vice-President offices fall vacant simultaneously?
options: The Chief Justice of India (or senior-most Judge of the Supreme Court) under the President (Discharge of Functions) Act, 1969
questions.explanation: Justice M. Hidayatullah (Chief Justice of India) was sworn in as acting President in 1969 when President Zakir Husain died and VP V.V. Giri resigned to contest elections.

questions.question: What is the maximum period of time within which an election must be held to fill a vacancy in the office of the President caused by death, resignation, or removal?
options: Within six months from the date of occurrence of the vacancy (Article 62(2))
questions.explanation: Article 62(2) mandates that an election to fill the vacancy must be completed within six months, during which the Vice-President acts as President.

questions.question: What is 'Pocket Veto' exercised by the President of India?
options: Keeping a Bill pending on the President's desk indefinitely without giving assent or returning it, because the Indian Constitution prescribes no time limit
questions.explanation: President Zail Singh exercised Pocket Veto on the Indian Post Office (Amendment) Bill in 1986. Because the Constitution specifies no deadline, 'the pocket of the Indian President is larger than that of the US President.'

polity_q5.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 5: Constitutional vs Statutory Bodies

questions.question: Which of the following is a CONSTITUTIONAL BODY explicitly established by an Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.explanation: Finance Commission is established under Article 280. NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional executive body; NHRC and CVC are statutory bodies created by Acts of Parliament.

questions.question: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India submits audit reports relating to the accounts of the Union to whom under Article 151?
options: To the President of India, who causes them to be laid before each House of Parliament
Directly to the Speaker of Lok Sabha
To the Public Accounts Committee Chairman
questions.explanation: Under Article 151(1), the CAG submits reports to the President (for the Union) and under Article 151(2) to the Governor (for the State).

questions.question: Which parliamentary committee is famously termed the 'Twin Sister' of the Estimates Committee, and works closely with the CAG?
questions.explanation: The PAC (consisting of 15 LS and 7 RS members) is described as the twin sister of the Estimates Committee; the CAG acts as the 'friend, philosopher, and guide' of the PAC.

questions.question: Under Article 324, what is the composition of the Election Commission of India?
options: The Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and such number of other Election Commissioners as the President may from time to time fix (currently 1 CEC + 2 ECs)
questions.explanation: Originally single-member, the ECI became a multi-member body in 1989 and permanently a 3-member body in 1993, with all commissioners having equal status and salary.

questions.question: Can an Election Commissioner be removed from office arbitrarily by the Government?
options: NO, under Article 324(5), an Election Commissioner can only be removed on the recommendation of the Chief Election Commissioner
By simple majority of Lok Sabha
questions.explanation: While the CEC can be removed only like a Supreme Court judge, other Election Commissioners enjoy protection against removal except on the CEC's recommendation.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution provides for the establishment of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC)?
questions.explanation: Article 338 establishes the NCSC; Article 338-A establishes the NCST (89th Amendment 2003); and Article 338-B establishes the NCBC (102nd Amendment 2018).

questions.question: What powers does the National Commission for Scheduled Castes (NCSC) have while investigating any complaint under Article 338(8)?
options: All the powers of a Civil Court trying a suit (summoning witnesses, requiring discovery of documents, receiving evidence on affidavits)
Powers of a Criminal Court to jail offenders
questions.explanation: The NCSC, NCST, and NCBC have all the procedural powers of a Civil Court under the Code of Civil Procedure (CPC) to summon officials and requisition records.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act bifurcated the combined National Commission for SCs and STs into two separate commissions?
questions.explanation: The 89th Amendment created the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under a new Article 338-A in 2003.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act granted constitutional status to the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC) by inserting Article 338-B?
questions.explanation: The 102nd Amendment conferred constitutional status on the NCBC, bringing it on par with NCSC and NCST.

questions.question: What is the constitutional body created under Article 279-A to make recommendations to the Union and States on Goods and Services Tax?
options: The Goods and Services Tax Council (GST Council)
questions.explanation: The GST Council, inserted by the 101st Amendment Act 2016, is chaired by the Union Finance Minister and includes State Finance Ministers.

questions.question: The Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) submits its annual report on its performance to whom under Article 323?
questions.explanation: Under Article 323(1), UPSC submits its report to the President, who causes it to be laid before Parliament along with a memorandum explaining non-acceptance of advice.

questions.question: Can a retired Chairman of the UPSC be appointed to any other post under the Government of India or a State Government under Article 319?
options: NO, the Chairman of the UPSC is ineligible for any further employment either under the Government of India or under a State Government
questions.explanation: Article 319 enforces strict post-retirement ineligibility on the UPSC Chairman to maintain absolute impartiality and integrity.

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed by the President?
options: Article 350-B (inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956)
questions.explanation: Article 350-B was inserted pursuant to the States Reorganisation Commission to investigate all matters relating to safeguards provided for linguistic minorities.

questions.question: Under which statutory Act was the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) established in India in 1993?
questions.explanation: The NHRC is a statutory body constituted on October 12, 1993, under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.

questions.question: Who heads the Selection Committee that recommends the appointment of the Chairperson and Members of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC)?
questions.explanation: Under Section 4 of PHRA, the committee is chaired by the Prime Minister and includes the Speaker of Lok Sabha, Union Home Minister, Leaders of Opposition in both Houses, and Deputy Chairman of Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: The Central Information Commission (CIC) is established under which statutory Act?
questions.explanation: The Central Information Commission was constituted in 2005 under Section 12 of the Right to Information Act, 2005.

questions.question: Under the RTI (Amendment) Act 2019, who determines the salaries, allowances, and term of office of Information Commissioners?
options: Equal to Election Commissioners (fixed in original Act)
questions.explanation: The 2019 amendment eliminated fixed 5-year terms and parity with Election Commissioners, vesting power in the Central Government to prescribe tenure and salary.

questions.question: Which statutory commission is responsible for monitoring the implementation of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act and RTE Act?
options: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
questions.explanation: NCPCR, established under the CPCR Act 2005, monitors child rights, RTE 2009, and POCSO 2012 implementation.

questions.question: What is the apex statutory body in India responsible for preventing and combating corruption in central government administration?
questions.explanation: The CVC was given statutory status by the CVC Act 2003, acting as an independent integrity watchdog free from executive control.

questions.question: Who exercises superintendence over the Delhi Special Police Establishment (CBI) in the investigation of offences committed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988?
questions.explanation: Under Section 8(1) of the CVC Act 2003, superintendence of the CBI regarding anti-corruption cases is vested in the CVC.

questions.question: Under which statutory Act is the 'Lokpal' for the Union and 'Lokayuktas' for the States established?
questions.explanation: The Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act 2013 established an anti-corruption ombudsman with jurisdiction over public functionaries, including the Prime Minister (with safeguards).

questions.question: Which was the first state in India to establish the institution of 'Lokayukta' in 1971?
questions.explanation: Maharashtra was the first state to operationalize the Lokayukta in 1971, although Odisha was the first to pass the legislation in 1970.

questions.question: Which agency under the Department of Revenue enforces the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) and Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA)?
questions.explanation: The Enforcement Directorate (ED), established in 1956, investigates financial crimes under PMLA 2002, FEMA 1999, and Fugitive Economic Offenders Act 2018.

questions.question: Is the 'National Development Council' (NDC) a constitutional or statutory body?
options: Neither constitutional nor statutory (it is an extra-constitutional executive body established by cabinet resolution in 1952)
questions.explanation: The NDC was established in August 1952 by an executive resolution of the Government to approve Five Year Plans, chaired by the Prime Minister.

questions.question: What is the constitutional body provided under Article 263 to investigate and discuss subjects of common interest between the Union and the States?
questions.explanation: The Inter-State Council was set up by Presidential Order in 1990 upon the recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission to strengthen cooperative federalism.

polity_q6.title: SSC CGL Polity PYQ - Set 6: Landmark SC Cases & Key Amendments

questions.question: The 'Basic Structure Doctrine' of the Indian Constitution was propounded by the Supreme Court in which landmark case decided on April 24, 1973?
options: Kesavananda Bharati v. State of Kerala (13-judge bench, 7-6 verdict)
Minerva Mills v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In Kesavananda Bharati, the largest bench in Indian judicial history (13 judges) ruled that Parliament's constituent power under Article 368 cannot alter the 'Basic Structure' of the Constitution.

questions.question: In which 1967 case had an 11-judge bench ruled that Parliament cannot amend or abridge any Fundamental Right under Part III?
options: I.C. Golaknath v. State of Punjab
Sajjan Singh v. State of Rajasthan
Shankari Prasad v. Union of India
questions.explanation: In Golaknath (1967), the Supreme Court ruled by a 6-5 majority that Fundamental Rights have a transcendental position and cannot be taken away by Article 368.

questions.question: Which landmark 1980 case struck down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368 (inserted by 42nd Amendment) that gave unlimited amending power to Parliament?
options: Minerva Mills v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Minerva Mills held that judicial review and the harmonious balance between Fundamental Rights and Directive Principles are fundamental to the Basic Structure.

questions.question: The 'Golden Triangle' of the Indian Constitution refers to which trinity of Fundamental Rights ensuring fairness and liberty?
questions.explanation: In the Maneka Gandhi case (1978), the Supreme Court ruled that Articles 14 (Equality), 19 (Freedom), and 21 (Life) are not isolated silos but form an interconnected 'Golden Triangle'.

questions.question: Which landmark 1978 case expanded Article 21 from mere 'Procedure Established by Law' to substantive 'Due Process of Law' (just, fair, and reasonable procedure)?
options: Maneka Gandhi v. Union of India
A.K. Gopalan v. State of Madras
Kharak Singh v. State of UP
questions.explanation: Overruling A.K. Gopalan (1950), Maneka Gandhi (1978) established that deprivation of personal liberty must follow a procedure that is right, just, and fair—not arbitrary.

questions.question: In which landmark 2017 case did a unanimous 9-judge bench declare the 'Right to Privacy' an intrinsic part of the Right to Life under Article 21?
options: Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India
questions.explanation: The Puttaswamy judgment unanimously overruled MP Sharma (1954) and Kharak Singh (1962), affirming privacy as a fundamental inalienable right in Part III.

questions.question: Which landmark 1992 case upheld 27% reservation for Other Backward Classes (OBCs) while establishing the 50% cap on total reservations and the 'Creamy Layer' exclusion?
options: Indra Sawhney v. Union of India (The Mandal Case)
M. Nagaraj v. Union of India
questions.explanation: A 9-judge bench ruled that reservations cannot exceed 50% except in extraordinary backward areas, and creamy layer individuals must be excluded from quotas.

questions.question: In which landmark 1994 case did a 9-judge bench establish that secularism is a basic feature of the Constitution and laid down strict limits on Article 356 (President's Rule)?
options: S.R. Bommai v. Union of India
questions.explanation: S.R. Bommai made presidential proclamations under Article 356 subject to judicial review, mandating floor tests in Legislative Assemblies as the only forum to prove majority.

questions.question: Which landmark 1997 Supreme Court judgment laid down mandatory workplace guidelines to prevent sexual harassment of women, later codified into the POSH Act 2013?
options: Mary Roy v. State of Kerala
questions.explanation: The Vishaka guidelines filled a legislative void using Article 21 and the CEDAW international convention until Parliament enacted the POSH Act in 2013.

questions.question: In which 1985 case did the Supreme Court grant maintenance to a divorced Muslim woman under Section 125 of CrPC, sparking national debates on Uniform Civil Code?
options: Mohd. Ahmed Khan v. Shah Bano Begum
questions.explanation: The Shah Bano judgment held that Section 125 CrPC is a secular criminal provision applicable to all citizens regardless of religion.

questions.question: In which 2017 case did a 5-judge Constitution Bench declare the practice of Instant Triple Talaq (Talaq-e-Biddat) unconstitutional and void?
options: Shayara Bano v. Union of India
questions.explanation: A 3-2 majority in Shayara Bano ruled that Talaq-e-Biddat is arbitrary, violating Article 14 of the Constitution.

questions.question: In which 2018 case did the Supreme Court decriminalize consensual adult homosexual relationships by reading down Section 377 of the IPC?
options: Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
questions.explanation: A 5-judge Constitution Bench unanimously held that Section 377 unconstitutionally discriminated against LGBTQ+ individuals on grounds of sex and dignity under Articles 14, 15, and 21.

questions.question: Which landmark 2015 judgment struck down Section 66A of the Information Technology Act, 2000 as unconstitutional for violating freedom of speech under Article 19(1)(a)?
options: Shreya Singhal v. Union of India
questions.explanation: Shreya Singhal struck down Section 66A, ruling that the chilling effect on online speech was overbroad and vague.

questions.question: The 'First Constitutional Amendment Act, 1951' inserted which Schedule to insulate land reform laws from judicial review?
questions.explanation: The 1st Amendment 1951, enacted by the provisional Parliament, inserted the Ninth Schedule, Articles 31A, and 31B, and added reasonable restrictions to Article 19(2).

questions.question: In which 2007 landmark case did a 9-judge bench rule that all laws placed in the Ninth Schedule after April 24, 1973 are open to judicial review if they violate the Basic Structure?
options: I.R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: The I.R. Coelho judgment held that there is no blanket immunity for Ninth Schedule laws added after the Kesavananda Bharati verdict date.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act is known as the 'Mini-Constitution' because of its vast, sweeping changes during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Amendment amended the Preamble, added Fundamental Duties (Part IV-A), inserted Part XIV-A (Tribunals), and increased the term of Lok Sabha from 5 to 6 years (later restored by 44th).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act removed the 'Right to Property' from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a Constitutional Legal Right under Article 300A?
questions.explanation: The Janata Party government's 44th Amendment repealed Articles 19(1)(f) and 31, inserting Article 300A in Part XII to ensure property is not a Fundamental Right.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act lowered the voting age in India from 21 years to 18 years for Lok Sabha and Assembly elections?
questions.explanation: The 61st Amendment amended Article 326 to expand youth democratic participation by lowering the voting age from 21 to 18.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the 10% reservation for Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) in education and public employment?
questions.explanation: The 103rd Amendment enabled 10% EWS reservation without disturbing the existing 50% SC/ST/OBC quota; upheld by Supreme Court in Janhit Abhiyan (2022).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act ended the provision for nominating two Anglo-Indians to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies?
questions.explanation: The 104th Amendment extended SC/ST reservation in legislatures for 10 years (until 2030) while discontinuing the nomination of Anglo-Indians under Articles 331 and 333.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act restored the power of State Governments to identify and maintain their own state lists of Socially and Educationally Backward Classes (SEBCs)?
questions.explanation: The 105th Amendment clarified that states retain powers to identify backward classes after the Supreme Court's Maratha reservation judgment.

questions.question: The 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam', providing 33% reservation for women in Lok Sabha and Assemblies, is which Constitutional Amendment Act?
questions.explanation: The 106th Amendment reserves 1/3 of all seats for women in Lok Sabha, State Assemblies, and Delhi Assembly for 15 years following the next delimitation exercise.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST) in India?
questions.explanation: The 101st Amendment introduced Article 246A (concurrent tax powers), Article 269A (IGST), and Article 279A (GST Council), rolling out GST on July 1, 2017.

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act gave constitutional status and protection to Co-operative Societies by adding Part IX-B and Article 43-B?
questions.explanation: The 97th Amendment added the right to form cooperatives in Article 19(1)(c), Article 43B in DPSP, and Part IX-B (partially struck down in 2021 regarding state cooperatives due to lack of state ratification).

questions.question: Which Constitutional Amendment Act capped the size of the Council of Ministers at 15% of the total strength of the Lower House (and minimum 12 ministers in States)?
questions.explanation: The 91st Amendment amended Articles 75 and 164 to limit the jumbo size of cabinets to 15% and tightened the Anti-Defection Law by deleting the one-third split protection.
